title.zh: 卷九十二 志第六十八 兵四
title.raw: 卷九十二 志第六十八 兵四 Volume 92 Treatises 68: Military 4

sentences.zh: 清理軍伍訓練賞功火器車船馬政

translations.literal: Clearing military rolls, training, rewards for merit, firearms, chariots and ships, and horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Clearing the rolls, drill, merit rewards, firearms, vehicles and ships, and horse policy.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，遣給事等官分閱天下軍，重定垛集軍更代法。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, he dispatched supervising secretaries and other officials to inspect troops throughout the realm by division, and re-established the law for rotation of rostered garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor came to the throne, he sent supervising secretaries and other officials to review troops across the empire in sections and redefined the system for rotating rostered garrison soldiers.

sentences.zh: 初，三丁已上，垛正軍一，別有貼戶，正軍死，貼戶丁補。

translations.literal: Initially, where there were three adult males or more, one was rostered as principal soldier; there was also a supplemental household; when the principal soldier died, a male from the supplemental household would fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in households with three adult males or more, one was registered as the principal soldier and another household served as supplemental; when the principal soldier died, a son from the supplemental household took his place.

sentences.zh: 至是，令正軍、貼戶更代，貼戶單丁者免；

translations.literal: At this time it was ordered that principal soldiers and supplemental households should rotate in service, and supplemental households with only one male were exempted;
translations.idiomatic: Now the court ordered principal soldiers and supplemental households to take turns on duty, while supplemental households with only one adult male were excused;

sentences.zh: 當軍家蠲其一丁徭。

translations.literal: military households were exempted from corvée for one male.
translations.idiomatic: and each household liable for military service had one man freed from labor levy.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，興州左屯衛軍範濟極言勾軍之擾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, Fan Ji, a soldier of the Left Garrison Guard at Xingzhou, spoke at length on the harassment caused by conscript-recruitment checks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, Fan Ji, a soldier of the Left Garrison Guard at Xingzhou, protested vigorously against the abuses of household conscript checks.

sentences.zh: 富峪衛百戶錢興奏言：「祖本涿鹿衛軍，死，父繼，以功授百戶。

translations.literal: Qian Xing, centurion of Fuyu Guard, memorialized: "My forebear was originally a soldier of Zhuolu Guard; when he died my father succeeded him and was appointed centurion for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xing, a centurion of Fuyu Guard, memorialized: "My grandfather had originally been a soldier of Zhuolu Guard; when he died my father succeeded him and was appointed centurion for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 臣已襲父職，而本衛猶以臣祖為逃軍，屢行勾取。」

translations.literal: I have already inherited my father's post, yet our guard still treats my grandfather as a deserter and repeatedly conducts conscript checks to seize him."
translations.idiomatic: I have already inherited my father's post, yet our guard still lists my grandfather as a deserter and repeatedly sends conscript officers to seize him."

sentences.zh: 帝謂尚書張本曰：「軍伍不清，弊多類此。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Minister Zhang Ben: "When military rolls are unclear, abuses are mostly of this kind."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Minister Zhang Ben: "When military registers are unclear, abuses are mostly of this kind."

sentences.zh: 已而宣宗立，軍弊益滋，黠者往往匿其籍，或誣攘良民充伍。

translations.literal: Before long the Xuande Emperor was enthroned; abuses in the military worsened, and the cunning often hid their registers or falsely seized innocent civilians to fill quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xuande Emperor came to the throne; military abuses grew worse, and the crafty often concealed their registers or falsely seized law-abiding civilians to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝諭兵部曰：「朝廷於軍民，如舟車任載，不可偏重。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed the Ministry of War: "The court's relation to soldiers and civilians is like a boat or cart bearing a load—neither side may be overweighted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor instructed the Ministry of War: "The court's relation to soldiers and civilians is like a boat or cart bearing a load—neither may be overburdened.

sentences.zh: 有司宜審實毋混。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials should verify facts and not mix categories."
translations.idiomatic: Responsible officials should verify the facts and not confuse categories."

sentences.zh: 乃分遣吏部侍郎黃宗載等清理天下軍衛。

translations.literal: Then Huang Zongzai, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and others were dispatched to clear military guards throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The court then dispatched Huang Zongzai, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and others to clear military guards throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 三年敕給事、御史清軍，定十一條例，榜示天下。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered supervising secretaries and censors to clear military rolls and established eleven regulations, posted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ordered supervising secretaries and censors to clear military rolls, fixed eleven regulations, and posted them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 明年復增為二十二條。

translations.literal: The next year they were increased to twenty-two articles.
translations.idiomatic: The following year these were expanded to twenty-two articles.

sentences.zh: 五年，從尚書張本請，令天下官吏、軍旗公勘自洪、永來勾軍之無蹤者，豁免之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, following Minister Zhang Ben's request, it was ordered that throughout the realm civil officials and military banner personnel jointly verify deserters conscripted since Hongwu and Yongle who left no trace, and exempt them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, at Minister Zhang Ben's request, civil officials and military banner officers throughout the realm were ordered jointly to verify deserters conscripted since the Hongwu and Yongle reigns who had left no trace, and to exempt them.

sentences.zh: 六年，令勾軍有親老疾獨子者，編之近地，餘丁赴工逋亡者例發口外，改為罰工一年，示優恤焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when conscripting soldiers, those whose families had aged parents, illness, or only sons were assigned to nearby districts; others who fled labor or went missing were previously sent beyond the passes—in this changed to one year of penal labor, showing preferential consideration.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when conscripting soldiers, those with aged parents, illness, or only sons in the family were assigned to nearby districts; others who fled labor service or went missing had previously been sent beyond the passes—now this was changed to one year of penal labor, as a mark of leniency.

sentences.zh: 八年，免蘇州衛抑配軍百五十九人，已食糧止令終其身者，千二百三十九人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, 159 soldiers forcibly assigned in Suzhou Guard were exempted; 1,239 who had already received rations were ordered to serve only for life.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, 159 soldiers forcibly assigned in Suzhou Guard were released, and 1,239 who had already been receiving rations were allowed to serve out their lives only.

sentences.zh: 先是，蘇、常軍戶絕者，株累族黨，動以千計，知府況鐘言於朝，又常州民訴受抑為軍者七百有奇，故特敕巡撫侍郎周忱清理。

translations.literal: Previously, when military households in Suzhou and Changzhou died out, clans were implicated en masse, often by thousands; Prefect Kuang Zhong spoke to court, and also Changzhou civilians petitioned that over seven hundred had been wrongly pressed into the military—hence a special edict to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Chen to clear records.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when military households in Suzhou and Changzhou died out, entire clans were implicated, often numbering in the thousands; Prefect Kuang Zhong spoke to the court, and Changzhou civilians also petitioned that more than seven hundred had been wrongly pressed into service—hence a special edict commissioning Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Chen to clear the records.

sentences.zh: 正統初，令勾軍家丁盡者，除籍；

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengtong, when a conscript household had no sons left, their register was struck;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengtong reign, when a conscript household had no male heirs left, its register was struck;

sentences.zh: 逃軍死亡及事故者，或家本軍籍，而偶同姓名，裏胥挾讎妄報冒解，或已解而赴部聲冤者，皆與豁免。

translations.literal: deserters who died and accident victims, or families originally on military registers but matched only by chance of same name—village clerks bearing grudges falsely reported to clear quotas—or those already cleared who appealed at the ministry—all were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: deserters who had died or perished by mischance, or families originally on military registers but matched only by a chance similarity of name—village clerks bearing grudges who falsely reported them cleared—or those already cleared who appealed at the ministry—all were exempted.

sentences.zh: 定例，補伍皆發極邊，而南北人互易。

translations.literal: The regulation fixed that replacements were all sent to the furthest borders, with northerners and southerners swapped.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed that replacements were all posted to the farthest frontiers, with northerners and southerners exchanged.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊士奇謂風土異宜，瀕於夭折，請從所宜發戍。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Shiqi said climates differ and men verge on early death, and asked that posting follow what suited each region.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Shiqi said that climates differ and men were liable to die young, and asked that posting follow what suited each region.

sentences.zh: 署兵部侍郎鄺埜以為紊祖制，寢之。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of War Kuang Ye held this would disrupt ancestral institutions and shelved it.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Vice Minister of War Kuang Ye held that this would disrupt ancestral institutions, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，山西巡撫李侃復請補近衛，始議行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua, Shanxi Grand Coordinator Li Kan again asked that replacements go to nearby guards; then it was agreed to implement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua, Shanxi Grand Coordinator Li Kan again asked that replacements be posted to nearby guards, and only then was the policy agreed upon.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命御史十一人分道清軍，以十分為率，及三分者最，不及者殿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, eleven censors were ordered to clear military rolls by separate circuits; on a scale of ten parts, those reaching three parts were rated best, those not were ranked last.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, eleven censors were ordered to clear military rolls along separate routes; on a scale of ten, those achieving three parts were rated highest and those falling short were ranked lowest.

sentences.zh: 時以罪謫者逃故，亦勾其家丁。

translations.literal: At the time the household members of those exiled for crime who fled were also conscripted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the household members of those exiled for crime who had fled were also subject to conscript checks.

sentences.zh: 御史江昂謂非「罰弗及嗣。」

translations.literal: Censor Jiang Ang said this was not in keeping with "punishment does not extend to heirs."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiang Ang said this was not in keeping with the principle that "punishment does not extend to heirs.

sentences.zh: 之義，乃禁之。

translations.literal: The meaning of this principle—and it was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: This did not accord with the principle that punishment does not extend to heirs, and the practice was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，捕亡令愈苛，有株累數十家，勾攝經數十年者，丁口已盡，猶移覆紛紜不已。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, orders to catch deserters grew harsher; some families of dozens were implicated; summons stretched over decades though mouths were exhausted, yet appeals and transfers still flew without end.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, orders to catch deserters grew harsher; some cases implicated dozens of households; conscript summons dragged on for decades though every mouth in the family was gone, yet appeals and transfers still flew without end.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書胡世甯請「屢經清報者免勾。

translations.literal: Minister of War Hu Shining requested: "Those repeatedly cleared in reports should be free from further conscript checks.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Hu Shining requested: "Those repeatedly cleared in official reports should be exempt from further conscript checks.

sentences.zh: 又避役之人必緩急難倚，急改編原籍。

translations.literal: Also those who dodge service cannot be relied on in emergency—quickly re-register them to original districts.
translations.idiomatic: Also, those who evade service cannot be relied on in an emergency—quickly re-register them to their original districts.

sentences.zh: 衛所有缺伍，則另選舍餘及犯罪者充補。

translations.literal: When guards have vacancies, separately select reserve lodge soldiers and criminals to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: When a guard has vacancies, separately select reserve lodge soldiers and criminals to fill them.

sentences.zh: 犯重發邊衛者，責賣家產，闔房遷發，使絕顧念。

translations.literal: Those guilty of serious crimes sent to border guards should be made to sell property and whole households relocated, to cut off hope of return.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of serious crimes sent to border guards should be made to sell their property and have their entire households relocated, to cut off any hope of return.

sentences.zh: 庶衛卒皆土著，而逃亡益鮮」。

translations.literal: Thus garrison soldiers would mostly be locals and deserters fewer."
translations.idiomatic: Thus garrison soldiers would mostly be locals and desertion would grow rare."

sentences.zh: 帝是其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 其後，用主事王學益議，制勾單，立法詳善。

translations.literal: Later, following Registrar Wang Xueyi's proposal, conscript check forms were instituted with detailed and sound law.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Registrar Wang Xueyi's proposal, standardized conscript forms were instituted and the regulations were drawn up in careful detail.

sentences.zh: 久之，停差清軍御史，寬管解逃軍及軍赴衛違限之科。

translations.literal: After long while, dispatch of censors to clear military rolls stopped, and penalties for escorting deserters and soldiers late to guards were relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, the dispatch of censors to clear military rolls ceased, and penalties for escorting deserters and for soldiers arriving late at their guards were relaxed.

sentences.zh: 清軍官日玩愒，文卷磨滅，議者復請申飭。

translations.literal: Clear-military officers grew negligent day by day, documents wore away, and advocates again asked for admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Officers charged with clearing military rolls grew negligent day by day, documents wore away, and advocates again asked that the regulations be enforced.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，給事中徐貞明言：「勾軍東南，資裝出於戶丁，解送出於裏遞，每軍不下百金。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli, Supervising Secretary Xu Zhenming said: "Southeast conscript checks—outfit costs come from household sons, escort from village relays, each soldier not less than one hundred taels.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wanli, Supervising Secretary Xu Zhenming said: "In the southeast, conscript checks—outfit costs fall on household sons and escort costs on village relays, and each soldier costs no less than one hundred taels.

sentences.zh: 大困東南之民，究無補於軍政。

translations.literal: Greatly straining the people of the southeast, ultimately of no help to military administration.
translations.idiomatic: This greatly burdens the people of the southeast and ultimately does nothing for military administration.

sentences.zh: 宜視班匠例，免其解補，而重徵班銀，以資召募，使東南永無勾補之擾，而西北之行伍亦充。」

translations.literal: Should follow the artisan-corvée precedent, exempt escort and replacement, levy heavier corvée silver for recruitment, so the southeast forever free of conscript trouble and northwest ranks full."
translations.idiomatic: We should follow the artisan-corvée precedent, exempt them from escort and replacement, levy heavier corvée silver to fund recruitment, so that the southeast is forever free of conscript harassment and the ranks in the northwest are also filled."

sentences.zh: 鄖陽巡撫王世貞因言有四便：應勾之戶，樂於就近，不圖避匿，便一；

translations.literal: Yunyang Grand Coordinator Wang Shizhen then said there were four conveniences: households liable gladly serve nearby, not hiding—convenience one;
translations.idiomatic: Yunyang Grand Coordinator Wang Shizhen then said there were four advantages: households liable for conscription would gladly serve nearby and not seek to hide—first advantage;

sentences.zh: 各安水土，不至困絕，便二；

translations.literal: each settles in native soil, not driven to ruin—convenience two;
translations.idiomatic: each would settle in his native region and not be driven to destitution—second advantage;

sentences.zh: 近則不逃，逃亦易追，便三；

translations.literal: near means no flight, easy pursuit—convenience three;
translations.idiomatic: posted nearby they would not flee, and if they fled they could easily be pursued—third advantage;

sentences.zh: 解戶不至破家，便四。

translations.literal: escort households not ruined—convenience four.
translations.idiomatic: escort households would not be ruined—fourth advantage.

sentences.zh: 而兵部卒格貞明議，不行。

translations.literal: But the Ministry of War finally blocked Xu Zhenming's proposal and did not implement it.
translations.idiomatic: But the Ministry of War ultimately blocked Xu Zhenming's proposal and did not implement it.

sentences.zh: 後十三年，南京兵部尚書郭應聘復請各就近地，南北改編。

translations.literal: Thirteen years later Nanjing Minister of War Guo Yingpin again asked each to be reassigned nearby, with north-south re-registration.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years later, Nanjing Minister of War Guo Yingpin again asked that each soldier be reassigned nearby, with north-south re-registration.

sentences.zh: 又言：「應勾之軍，南直隸至六萬六千餘，株連至二三十萬人，請自天順以前竟與釋免」。

translations.literal: Also: "Soldiers liable in south Zhili exceed 66,000, implicating 200,000 to 300,000—ask release all before Tianshun."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Soldiers liable for conscription in south Zhili number more than sixty-six thousand, with as many as two or three hundred thousand implicated by kinship—please release them all for cases before the Tianshun reign."

sentences.zh: 報可，遠近皆悅。

translations.literal: Approved; near and far all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved, and people near and far were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 然改編令下，求改者相繼。

translations.literal: Yet when the re-registration order was issued, seekers to change kept coming in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once the re-registration order was issued, petitioners seeking reassignment came one after another.

sentences.zh: 明年，兵部言：「什伍漸耗，邊鎮軍人且希圖脫伍」。

translations.literal: The next year the Ministry of War said: "Companies are thinning; border-garrison soldiers moreover hope to shed their rolls."
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Ministry of War reported: "Companies are thinning, and border-garrison soldiers are even hoping to shed their rolls."

sentences.zh: 有旨復舊，而應聘之議復不行。

translations.literal: An edict restored the old rules, and Guo Yingpin's proposal again was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the former rules, and Guo Yingpin's proposal again was not implemented.

sentences.zh: 凡軍衛掌於職方，而勾清則武庫主之。

translations.literal: Generally military guards were managed by the Bureau of Appointments, while conscript clearing was presided over by the Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, military guards fell under the Bureau of Appointments, while conscript clearing was handled by the Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 有所勾攝，自衛所開報，先核鄉貫居止，內府給批，下有司提本軍，謂之跟捕；

translations.literal: When there was conscription, the guard reported; native place and residence were first verified, the inner court issued a warrant, and the local office seized the soldier himself—called genbu, tracking capture;
translations.idiomatic: When conscription was required, the guard reported it; native place and residence were first verified, the inner court issued a warrant, and the local office seized the soldier himself—called tracking capture;

sentences.zh: 提家丁，謂之勾捕。

translations.literal: seizing household members was called goubu, conscript capture.
translations.idiomatic: seizing household members was called conscript capture.

sentences.zh: 間有恩恤開伍者。

translations.literal: Occasionally grace opened vacancies in the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally imperial grace opened vacancies in the rolls.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十三年，令應補軍役生員，遣歸卒業。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu, students liable for military service were ordered sent home to complete their studies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu, students liable for military replacement were ordered sent home to complete their studies.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年，上虞人李志道充楚雄衛軍，死，有孫宗皋宜繼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande, Li Zhidao of Shangyu filled service as soldier of Chuxiong Guard; he died, and his grandson Zonggao should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuande, Li Zhidao of Shangyu had served as a soldier of Chuxiong Guard; when he died, his grandson Zonggao was due to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 時已中鄉試，尚書張本言於帝，得免。

translations.literal: He had already passed the provincial examination; Minister Zhang Ben spoke to the Emperor, and exemption was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He had already passed the provincial examination; Minister Zhang Ben spoke to the Emperor, and he was exempted.

sentences.zh: 如此者絕少。

translations.literal: Such cases were extremely few.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases were exceedingly rare.

sentences.zh: 戶有軍籍，必仕至兵部尚書始得除。

translations.literal: A household with a military register had to serve to Minister of War before removal.
translations.idiomatic: A household on the military register had to produce an official who rose to Minister of War before the register could be removed.

sentences.zh: 軍士應起解者，皆僉妻；

translations.literal: Soldiers to be escorted to post all took wives;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who were to be escorted to their posts all took wives;

sentences.zh: 有津給軍裝、解軍行糧、軍丁口糧之費。

translations.literal: there were allowances for kit, escort travel grain, and dependents' grain.
translations.idiomatic: and there were allowances for kit, travel grain for the escort, and grain for dependents.

sentences.zh: 其冊單編造皆有恆式。

translations.literal: Compilation of registers and slips all had fixed forms.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation of registers and slips all followed fixed forms.

sentences.zh: 初定戶口、收軍、勾清三冊。

translations.literal: Initially three registers were fixed: household, receiving soldiers, and conscript clearing.
translations.idiomatic: Initially three registers were established: household rolls, receiving soldiers, and conscript clearing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十一年，又編四冊，曰軍貫，曰兜底，曰類衛、類姓。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Jiajing, four more were compiled, called military pedigree, bottom-cover, by guard, and by surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Jiajing, four more were compiled, called military pedigree, bottom-cover, by guard, and by surname.

sentences.zh: 其勾軍另給軍單。

translations.literal: For conscript checks a separate military slip was issued.
translations.idiomatic: For conscript checks a separate military slip was issued.

sentences.zh: 蓋終明世，于軍籍最嚴。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming, military registers were strictest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Ming dynasty, military registers were enforced more strictly than any other.

sentences.zh: 然弊政漸叢，而擾民日甚。

translations.literal: Yet abuses gradually piled up and harassment of the people worsened day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet abuses gradually accumulated and harassment of the people grew worse day by day.

sentences.zh: 明太祖起布衣，策羣力，取天下。

translations.literal: The Ming Taizu rose from commoner cloth, marshaled collective strength, and took the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming founder rose from commoner origins, marshaled collective strength, and won the realm.

sentences.zh: 即位後，屢命元勳宿將分道練兵，而其制未定。

translations.literal: After enthronement he repeatedly ordered meritorious veterans to train troops by route, yet the system was not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: After his enthronement he repeatedly ordered meritorious veterans to train troops along separate routes, yet the system was not fixed.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，命中書省、大都督府、御史臺、六部議教練軍士律：「騎卒必善馳射槍刀，步兵必善弓弩槍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, he ordered the Secretariat, Grand Marshal's Office, Censorate, and Six Ministries to deliberate regulations for training soldiers: "Cavalry must excel at mounted archery, spear, and saber; infantry must excel at bow, crossbow, and spear.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongwu, he ordered the Secretariat, the Grand Marshal's Office, the Censorate, and the Six Ministries to deliberate regulations for training soldiers: "Cavalry must excel at mounted archery, spear, and saber; infantry must excel at bow, crossbow, and spear.

sentences.zh: 射以十二矢之半，遠可到，近可中為程。

translations.literal: For archery, half of twelve arrows—far must reach, near must hit as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: For archery, with half of twelve arrows, the standard was that the far shot must reach its mark and the near shot must hit.

sentences.zh: 遠可到，將弁百六十步、軍士百二十步；

translations.literal: For far reach, officers 160 paces, soldiers 120;
translations.idiomatic: For the far shot, officers 160 paces and soldiers 120;

sentences.zh: 近可中，五十步。

translations.literal: for near hit, fifty paces.
translations.idiomatic: for the near shot, fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 彀弩以十二矢之五，遠可到，蹶張八十步，劃車一百五十步；

translations.literal: For crossbow, five of twelve arrows far reach—drawn bow 80 paces, carriage crossbow 150;
translations.idiomatic: For the crossbow, with five of twelve arrows for the far shot, the drawn bow 80 paces and the carriage crossbow 150;

sentences.zh: 近可中，蹶張四十步，劃車六十步。

translations.literal: for near hit, drawn bow 40, carriage crossbow 60.
translations.idiomatic: for the near shot, the drawn bow 40 paces and the carriage crossbow 60.

sentences.zh: 槍必進退熟習。

translations.literal: Spear must be practiced in advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Spear drill must be practiced thoroughly in advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 在京衛所，以五千人為率，取五之一，指揮以下官領赴御前驗試，餘以次番試。

translations.literal: In capital guards, per 5,000 as standard, one fifth taken; officers from commander down led them to imperial review, the rest tried in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital guards, for every five thousand men one fifth was selected; officers from commander down led them to trial before the throne, and the rest were tested in rotation.

sentences.zh: 在外都司衛所，每衛五千人，取五之一，千戶以下官領赴京驗試。

translations.literal: In outer regional commands and guards, each guard 5,000, one fifth taken; officers below qianhu led them to capital for review.
translations.idiomatic: In regional commands and guards outside the capital, for each guard of five thousand one fifth was selected; officers below the rank of qianhu led them to the capital for review.

sentences.zh: 餘以次番試。

translations.literal: The rest tried in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder were tested in rotation.

sentences.zh: 軍士步騎皆善，將領各以其能受賞，否則罰。

translations.literal: If infantry and cavalry were all skilled, officers were each rewarded according to ability; otherwise punished.
translations.idiomatic: If both infantry and cavalry were skilled, officers were rewarded according to their ability; otherwise they were punished.

sentences.zh: 軍士給錢六百為道里費。

translations.literal: Soldiers were given 600 cash as travel expense.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were given six hundred cash as travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 將領自指揮使以下，所統軍士三分至六分不中者，次第奪俸；

translations.literal: Officers from commander down—if 30% to 60% of troops under command failed, salaries were reduced by degrees;
translations.idiomatic: For officers from commander down, if thirty to sixty percent of the troops under their command failed, salaries were reduced by degrees;

sentences.zh: 七分以上，次第降官至為軍止。

translations.literal: 70% or more, demoted stepwise down to common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: if seventy percent or more failed, they were demoted step by step down to common soldier.

sentences.zh: 都指揮軍士四分以上不中，奪俸一年；

translations.literal: Regional commanders: if 40% or more of soldiers failed, salary seized for one year;
translations.idiomatic: For regional commanders, if forty percent or more of their soldiers failed, their salary was withheld for one year;

sentences.zh: 六分以上罷職。」

translations.literal: 60% or more, dismissed from office."
translations.idiomatic: if sixty percent or more failed, they were dismissed from office."

sentences.zh: 後十六年，令天下衛所善射者十選一，於農隙分番赴京較閱，以優劣為千百戶賞罰，邊軍本衛較射。

translations.literal: Sixteen years later, ordered throughout guards that one in ten skilled archers, in agricultural slack seasons rotate to capital for comparison, with rewards and punishments for centurions by excellence or failure; border troops tested in home guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen years later, he ordered that throughout the guards one skilled archer in ten, during agricultural slack seasons, should rotate to the capital for comparison, with centurions rewarded or punished by their men's performance; border troops were tested in their home guards.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命衛士習射於午門丹墀。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, ordered guard soldiers to practice archery at the Meridian Gate terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, he ordered guard soldiers to practice archery on the terrace before the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 明年復令：「天下衛所馬步軍士，各分十班，將弁以廕敘久次升者統之，冬月至京閱試。

translations.literal: The next year again ordered: "All guards' horse and foot soldiers, each divided into ten classes; officers promoted by hereditary seniority lead them; in winter month to capital for review.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again ordered: "All horse and foot soldiers of the guards, each divided into ten classes, led by officers promoted by hereditary seniority; in the winter month they come to the capital for review.

sentences.zh: 指揮、千百戶，年深慣戰及屯田者免。

translations.literal: Commanders and centurions—long service veterans skilled in battle and colonizers were exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and centurions who were long-service veterans skilled in battle or engaged in military colonies were exempt.

sentences.zh: 仍先下操練法，俾遵行。

translations.literal: Still first issue drill regulations for them to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Drill regulations were first issued for them to follow.

sentences.zh: 不如法及不嫻習者，罰。」

translations.literal: Those not per regulations or unskilled were punished."
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not meet the regulations or were unskilled were punished."

sentences.zh: 明年，詔五軍府：「比試軍士分三等賞鈔，又各給鈔三錠為路費，不中者亦給之。

translations.literal: The next year edict to Five Armies: "Compare soldiers in three grades reward paper notes, also each given three notes as travel expense; failures also given.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict to the Five Armies: "Soldiers in the comparison shall be rewarded with paper notes in three grades, and each shall also be given three notes for travel expenses; even those who fail shall receive them.

sentences.zh: 明年再試不如式，軍移戍雲南，官謫從徵，總小旗降為軍。

translations.literal: Next year if again failing the form, soldiers transferred to garrison Yunnan, officers demoted to campaign service, squad leaders reduced to common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: If they failed the standard again the next year, soldiers were transferred to garrison duty in Yunnan, officers were demoted to campaign service, and squad leaders were reduced to common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 武臣子弟襲職，試騎步射不中程，令還衛署事，與半俸，二年後仍試如故者，亦降為軍。」

translations.literal: Military heirs inheriting office—fail mounted and foot archery standard, ordered back to guard to handle affairs with half salary; two years later still as before on trial, also demoted to soldier."
translations.idiomatic: When military heirs inherited office, if they failed the mounted and foot archery standard they were ordered back to their guard to handle affairs on half salary; if after two years they still failed as before, they too were demoted to common soldiers."

sentences.zh: 景泰初，立十團營。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, Ten Corps Camps were established.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, the Ten Corps Camps were established.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄧林進《軒轅圖》，即古八陣法也，因用以教軍。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Deng Lin presented the 《Xuanyuan Diagram》, which is the ancient Eight Formations method, and it was used to teach troops.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Deng Lin presented the 《Xuanyuan Diagram》, which embodied the ancient Eight Formations, and it was used to train the troops.

sentences.zh: 成化間，增團營為十二，命月二次會操，起仲春十五日，止仲夏十五日，秋、冬亦如之。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, corps camps increased to twelve; ordered joint drill twice monthly, starting mid-spring fifteenth day to mid-summer fifteenth, autumn and winter likewise.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign the corps camps were increased to twelve; joint drill was ordered twice a month, from the fifteenth day of mid-spring to the fifteenth day of mid-summer, and likewise in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年，兵部尚書馬文升申明洪、永操法，五日內，二日走陣下營，三日演武。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi, the Minister of War Ma Wensheng clarified the training methods of the Hongwu and Yongle reigns: within five days, two days for marching formations and making camp, three days for martial drills.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Hongzhi, Minister of War Ma Wensheng reissued the Hongwu and Yongle drill regulations: over every five-day cycle, two days were for marching in formation and pitching camp, and three for field exercises.

sentences.zh: 武宗好武勇，每令提督坐營官操練，又自執金鼓演四鎮卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong loved martial valor; he often ordered the supervising camp officers to drill the troops, and himself took up gongs and drums to drill the soldiers of the four garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong delighted in martial display. He regularly ordered the officers who supervised the capital garrisons to drill their men, and he himself beat the gongs and drums while reviewing troops from the four metropolitan camps.

sentences.zh: 然大要以恣馳騁、供嬉戲，非有實也。

translations.literal: Yet for the most part this was to indulge free riding and provide amusement; there was no real substance to it.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part, however, these exercises served only to indulge his love of horsemanship and provide sport—they had little practical value.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年定，下營佈陣，止用三疊陣及四門方營。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing it was fixed that when breaking camp and deploying formations, only the three-tier formation and the four-gate square camp were to be used.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing it was decreed that when troops broke camp and formed up for battle, they might use only the three-deep formation and the four-gate square encampment.

sentences.zh: 又令每營選槍刀箭牌銃手各一二人為教師，轉相教習。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that each camp select one or two spearmen, swordsmen, archers, shield-bearers, and musketeers as instructors, who would teach one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Each camp was also to choose one or two skilled spearmen, swordsmen, archers, shield-bearers, and musketeers as drillmasters, who would train one another in rotation.

sentences.zh: 及更營制，分兵三十枝，設將三十員，各統三千人訓練，擇精銳者名選鋒，厚其校藝之賞。

translations.literal: When the camp system was reformed, troops were divided into thirty branches, thirty generals were appointed, each commanding three thousand men in training; the elite were named Selected Vanguard, and rewards for skill contests were made generous.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison system was reorganized, the army was split into thirty divisions under thirty commanders, each training three thousand men. The finest troops were designated Selected Vanguard, and prizes for martial competition were set at a generous rate.

sentences.zh: 總督大臣一月會操者四，餘日營將分練。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator held joint drills four times a month; on the remaining days the camp commanders trained separately.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator convened full musters four times each month; on other days the camp commanders drilled their units separately.

sentences.zh: 協理大臣及巡視給事、御史隨意入一營，校閱賞罰，因以擇選鋒。

translations.literal: The coordinating ministers, as well as inspecting supervising secretaries and censors, might enter any camp at will to review, reward, and punish, and thereby select vanguard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinating ministers, touring supervising secretaries, and censors might inspect any camp at will, confer rewards and punishments, and in the process choose men for the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 帝又置內營於內教場，練諸內使。

translations.literal: The emperor also established an inner camp at the inner training ground to drill the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also set up an inner camp on the palace drill field to train the eunuch guards.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，命各營將領以教練軍士分數多寡為黜陟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, each camp commander was ordered to be promoted or demoted according to how fully his troops were trained.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longqing reign, camp commanders were to be promoted or demoted according to how thoroughly they had trained their soldiers.

sentences.zh: 全營教練者加都督僉事，以次減；

translations.literal: Those whose entire camp was trained were promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief; rewards diminished step by step below that.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders whose whole camp was properly drilled could be raised to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief; lesser degrees of success brought proportionally smaller advancement.

sentences.zh: 全不教練者降祖職一級，革任回衛。

translations.literal: Those who did no training at all were demoted one level in hereditary rank, stripped of office, and returned to their guard post.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed to drill their men at all were reduced one step in hereditary rank, removed from command, and sent back to their home garrison.

sentences.zh: 三年內教練有成，操協大臣獎諭恩錄；

translations.literal: Within three years, if inner-camp training achieved results, the drill-coordinating ministers received commendations and special honors.
translations.idiomatic: If the inner camp produced tangible results within three years, the ministers who coordinated the drills were commended and granted special imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 無功績者議罰。

translations.literal: Those without achievement were subject to disciplinary punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who showed no results were liable to disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 規制雖立，然將卒率媮惰，操演徒為具文。

translations.literal: Though regulations were established, officers and soldiers were generally slack and lazy, and drills were empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were on the books, but officers and men were for the most part negligent and idle, and field exercises remained little more than paper compliance.

sentences.zh: 先是，浙江參將戚繼光以善教士聞，嘗調士兵，制鴛鴦陣破倭。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi Jiguang, deputy commander of Zhejiang, had been famed for skilled training of troops; he had once drilled militia and devised the Mandarin Duck Formation to break the Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Qi Jiguang, deputy commander in Zhejiang, had won renown for training soldiers. He had drilled local militia and devised the Mandarin Duck Formation to defeat the wokou.

sentences.zh: 至是已官總兵。

translations.literal: By this time he had already been appointed regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already risen to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 穆宗從給事中吳時來請，命繼光練兵薊門。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, acceding to the request of Supervising Secretary Wu Shilai, ordered Qi Jiguang to train troops at the Ji garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At the urging of Supervising Secretary Wu Shilai, Emperor Muzong ordered Qi Jiguang to train troops on the Ji frontier.

sentences.zh: 薊兵精整者數十年。

translations.literal: The Ji garrison troops remained well-disciplined for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji garrison remained a model of discipline for decades.

sentences.zh: 繼光嘗著《練兵實紀》以訓士。

translations.literal: Qi Jiguang once wrote the Records for Practicing Troops to instruct his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jiguang wrote the Records for Practicing Troops to instruct his men.

sentences.zh: 一曰練伍，首騎，次步，次車，次輜重；

translations.literal: The first topic is training the squad: cavalry first, then infantry, then chariots, then baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: The first subject was training the squad—cavalry first, then infantry, then chariots, then supply trains.

sentences.zh: 先選伍，次較藝，總之以合營。

translations.literal: First select squads, then compare skills, summing up in unified camp training.
translations.idiomatic: Squads were to be chosen first, skills tested next, and the whole brought together in camp-level coordination.

sentences.zh: 二曰練膽氣，使明作止進退及上下統屬、相友相助之義。

translations.literal: Second is training courage and spirit, making them understand the meaning of advance and halt, movement and withdrawal, command hierarchy above and below, and mutual friendship and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Second came training courage and morale—teaching men when to move and halt, advance and withdraw, how command ran from above to below, and how comrades were to support one another.

sentences.zh: 三曰練耳目，使明號令。

translations.literal: Third is training ears and eyes, making them understand signals and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Third was training ears and eyes, so that every signal and order would be understood.

sentences.zh: 四曰練手足，使熟技藝。

translations.literal: Fourth is training hands and feet, making them proficient in techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth was training hands and feet, until every man mastered his craft.

sentences.zh: 五曰練營陣，詳佈陣起行、結營及交鋒之正變。

translations.literal: Fifth is training camp formations, detailing the proper and variant forms of array deployment, marching out, encamping, and engaging the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth was training camp formations—the standard and variant methods of drawing up battle lines, marching out, making camp, and closing with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 終之以練將。

translations.literal: It concludes with training the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The work ended with the training of officers.

sentences.zh: 後多遵用之。

translations.literal: Later generations largely followed and applied it.
translations.idiomatic: Later commanders largely adopted and followed it.

sentences.zh: 賞功之制，太祖時，大賞平定中原、徵南諸將及雲南、越州之功。

translations.literal: As for the system of rewarding merit, in the time of the Founding Emperor, great rewards were given for pacifying the Central Plains, the southern campaigns, and the achievements in Yunnan and Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the reward system, the founding emperor had lavished great honors on the generals who pacified the Central Plains, conquered the south, and won victories in Yunnan and Yue.

sentences.zh: 賞格雖具，然不豫為令。

translations.literal: Though reward scales were drawn up, they were not established in advance as fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Reward tables were drawn up, but no standing rules were fixed in advance.

sentences.zh: 惟二十九年命沿海衛所指揮千百戶獲倭一船及賊者，升一級，賞銀五十兩，鈔五十錠，軍士水陸擒殺賊，賞銀有差。

translations.literal: Only in the twenty-ninth year an order was issued: coastal guard and battalion commanders and company officers who captured one Japanese pirate ship and its crew would be promoted one rank, rewarded fifty taels of silver and fifty ingots of paper money; soldiers who captured or killed pirates on land or sea received silver rewards in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the twenty-ninth year of his reign was an order issued: any guard or battalion commander, or company officer, who seized a pirate vessel and its crew would rise one rank and receive fifty taels of silver and fifty ingots of paper money; ordinary soldiers who captured or killed pirates on land or at sea were paid silver according to a graded scale.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以將士久勞，命禮部依太祖升賞例，參酌行之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, because officers and soldiers had labored long, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to draw on the Founding Emperor's promotion-and-reward precedents and implement them with appropriate adjustments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign, because troops had borne long hardship, the Ministry of Rites was told to follow the founding emperor's precedents for promotion and reward, adapting them as needed.

sentences.zh: 乃分奇功、首功、次功三等，其賞之輕重次第，率臨時取旨，亦不豫為令。

translations.literal: Then extraordinary merit, first merit, and second merit were divided into three grades; the sequence of heavy and light rewards was generally determined by imperial order on the spot, and again was not fixed in advance as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was then divided into three grades—extraordinary, first, and second—and the scale of reward was usually decided on the spot by imperial order, still without any permanent statute.

sentences.zh: 十二年定：「凡交鋒之際，突出敵背殺敗賊眾者，勇敢入陣斬將搴旗者，本隊已勝、別隊勝負未決、而能救援克敵者，受命能任事、出奇破賊成功者，皆為奇功。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year it was fixed: "At the moment of engagement, those who burst out behind the enemy's rear and defeat the bandits; those who boldly enter the formation to behead generals and seize banners; those who, when their own unit has already won but another unit's outcome is undecided, can go to the rescue and overcome the enemy; those who receive orders and can fulfill tasks, using unexpected tactics to break the enemy and succeed—all count as extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the standard was set: "In the heat of battle, extraordinary merit went to the man who broke out behind the enemy and routed them; who charged into the enemy line to behead a commander or seize a banner; who, though his own unit had already prevailed, rescued a neighboring unit still locked in combat and turned defeat into victory; or who, entrusted with a mission, carried it through with an unexpected stroke that broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 齊力前進、首先敗賊者，前隊交鋒未決、後隊向前敗賊者，皆為首功。

translations.literal: Those who advance together with full force and are first to defeat the enemy, and those who, when the front rank's engagement is undecided, press forward from the rear rank to defeat the enemy—all count as first merit.
translations.idiomatic: First merit went to those who pressed forward in concert and were the first to break the enemy, or who, when the front line was still locked in combat, drove forward from the rear and turned the tide.

sentences.zh: 軍行及營中擒獲奸細者，亦準首功。

translations.literal: Those who capture spies while on march or in camp also count as first merit.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing enemy spies on the march or in camp also counted as first merit.

sentences.zh: 餘皆次功。」

translations.literal: All others count as second merit.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else fell under second merit.

sentences.zh: 又立功賞勘合，定四十字，曰：「神威精勇猛，強壯毅英雄。

translations.literal: Merit verification tallies were also established, fixed at forty characters, reading: "Divine prowess, refined courage, fierce and strong; resolute, heroic.
translations.idiomatic: Merit certificates were also issued, numbered by a fixed forty-character code that began: "Divine prowess, refined courage, fierce and strong; resolute, heroic.

sentences.zh: 克勝兼超捷，奇功奮銳鋒。

translations.literal: Conquering victory combined with surpassing agility; extraordinary merit exerting sharp vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Conquering victory with surpassing speed; extraordinary merit driving the sharp vanguard.

sentences.zh: 智謀宣妙略，剛烈效忠誠。

translations.literal: Wisdom and strategy deploying subtle stratagems; stern integrity rendering loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom and strategy deploying subtle plans; stern integrity proving loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 果敢能安定，揚名顯大勳。」

translations.literal: Bold and resolute, able to bring stability; spreading fame and displaying great achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resolute, able to restore order; spreading one's name and displaying great merit."

sentences.zh: 編號用寶，貯內府印綬監。

translations.literal: Numbers were assigned with the imperial seal, and the tallies were stored in the Directorate of Seals and Registers within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Each tally was stamped with the imperial seal and kept in the Directorate of Seals and Registers inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 當是時，稽功之法甚嚴。

translations.literal: At that time, the method of verifying merit was very strict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the verification of merit was extremely rigorous.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年，造賞功牌，有奇功、頭功、齊力之分，以大臣主之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, merit-reward plaques were made, with distinctions of extraordinary merit, head merit, and combined-effort merit, overseen by a senior official.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong merit plaques were cast in three classes—extraordinary merit, head merit, and combined-effort merit—under the supervision of a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 凡挺身突陣斬將奪旗者，與奇功牌。

translations.literal: All who boldly charged the formation to behead generals and seize banners received the extraordinary-merit plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who charged the enemy line to behead a commander or seize a banner received the extraordinary-merit plaque.

sentences.zh: 生擒瓦剌或斬首一級，與頭功牌。

translations.literal: Those who captured Oirats alive or took one enemy head received the head-merit plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing an Oirat alive or taking a single enemy head earned the head-merit plaque.

sentences.zh: 雖無功而被傷者，與齊力牌。

translations.literal: Even those who performed no merit but were wounded received the combined-effort plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Even a man who won no other distinction but was wounded in action received the combined-effort plaque.

sentences.zh: 蓋專為瓦剌入犯設也。

translations.literal: This was specifically established for the Oirat invasion.
translations.idiomatic: The system had been created specifically for the Oirat invasion.

sentences.zh: 是後，將士功賞視立功之地，準例奏行。

translations.literal: Afterward, rewards for officers and soldiers were assessed according to where merit was earned, and submitted and implemented according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, officers and soldiers were rewarded according to the theater in which they had earned merit, each case reported and carried out under the applicable precedent.

sentences.zh: 北邊為上，東北邊次之，西番及苗蠻又次之，內地反賊又次之。

translations.literal: The northern frontier ranked highest, the northeast frontier next, western barbarians and Miao rebels after that, and internal rebels lowest.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier ranked first, the northeast second, campaigns against western tribes and Miao bandits third, and suppression of internal rebels last.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，苦倭甚，故海上功比北邊尤為最。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Shizong, suffering from the Japanese pirates was severe, so maritime merit ranked even above the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong the wokou scourge was so severe that merit won at sea ranked even above that on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 北邊，自甘肅迤東，抵山海關。

translations.literal: The northern frontier, from Gansu eastward to Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier ran from Gansu eastward to Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年例：「一人斬一級者，進一秩，至三秩止。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year of Chenghua precedent: "One man beheading one head advances one rank, up to three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua fourteen precedent held: "A soldier who alone beheaded one enemy rose one rank, to a maximum of three ranks.

sentences.zh: 二人共斬者，為首進秩同。

translations.literal: Two men jointly beheading—the leader's rank advancement is the same.
translations.idiomatic: If two men shared a kill, the leader received the same promotion.

sentences.zh: 壯男與實授，幼弱婦女與署職。

translations.literal: Adult males receive substantive appointment; children, women, and the weak receive acting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Heads taken from adult males brought substantive rank; those from children, women, or the infirm brought acting rank only.

sentences.zh: 為從及四級以上，俱給賞。

translations.literal: Followers and those at the fourth rank and above all receive monetary reward.
translations.idiomatic: Assistants in the kill, and all men from the fourth rank upward, received cash reward instead.

sentences.zh: 領軍官部下五百人者，獲五級，進一秩。

translations.literal: Commanding officers with five hundred men under them—for five heads obtained, advance one rank.
translations.idiomatic: An officer commanding five hundred men who accounted for five enemy heads in his unit rose one rank.

sentences.zh: 領千人者，倍之。」

translations.literal: Those commanding a thousand men—double that.
translations.idiomatic: One commanding a thousand needed twice that number.

sentences.zh: 正德十年重定例：「獨斬一級者升一秩。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhende the precedent was revised: "One who alone beheads one head is promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhengde the rule was revised: "A man who alone beheaded one enemy was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 三人共者，首升署一秩，從給賞。

translations.literal: When three share jointly—the leader receives one acting rank, followers receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: When three shared a kill, the leader received one acting rank and the others cash.

sentences.zh: 四五六人共者，首給賞，從量賞。

translations.literal: When four, five, or six share jointly—the leader receives reward, followers receive scaled reward.
translations.idiomatic: When four, five, or six shared, the leader received the cash award and the rest a reduced share.

sentences.zh: 二人共斬一幼敵者，首視三人例，從量賞。

translations.literal: When two jointly behead one young enemy—the leader is treated under the three-man rule, followers receive scaled reward.
translations.idiomatic: If two men together beheaded a youth, the leader was rewarded under the three-man rule and the assistant at a reduced rate.

sentences.zh: 不願升者，每實授一秩，賞銀五十兩，署職二十兩。」

translations.literal: Those unwilling to accept promotion—for each substantive rank, fifty taels of silver reward; for acting rank, twenty taels.
translations.idiomatic: Men who declined promotion received fifty taels of silver for each substantive rank forfeited, or twenty for each acting rank."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年定，領軍官千、把總，加至三秩止，都指揮以上，止升署職二級，餘加賞。

translations.literal: Fixed in the fifteenth year of Jiajing: regimental commanders and platoon leaders could be promoted up to three ranks at most; regional commanders and above received only two acting ranks, with the rest in additional reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing it was fixed that company and platoon commanders might rise no more than three ranks; regional commanders and above received at most two acting ranks, with any further merit paid out in silver.

sentences.zh: 東北邊，初定三級當北邊之一。

translations.literal: Northeast frontier—initially three heads counted as one northern frontier head.
translations.idiomatic: On the northeast frontier, three enemy heads initially counted as one on the northern standard.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，改與北邊同。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period this was changed to equal the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli this was changed to parity with the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 番寇苗蠻，亦三級進一秩，實授署職，視北邊。

translations.literal: Barbarian bandits and Miao rebels—also three heads for one rank promotion; substantive and acting appointments follow the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Against frontier tribes and Miao bandits, three heads likewise earned one rank, with substantive and acting appointments calculated as on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 十級以上並不及數者給賞。

translations.literal: Ten heads and above, or failing to reach the required number, receive monetary reward.
translations.idiomatic: Ten heads or more, or totals falling short of the quota, were rewarded in cash.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，令陝西番寇功，視成化中例，軍官千總領五百人者，部下斬三十級，領千人者六十級，把總領五百人者十級，領千人者三十級，俱進一秩，至三秩止。

translations.literal: Third year of Wanli—ordered that merit against Shaanxi barbarian bandits follow the Chenghua precedent: regimental commanders leading five hundred—thirty heads from subordinates; leading a thousand—sixty heads; platoon leaders leading five hundred—ten heads; leading a thousand—thirty heads—all advance one rank, up to three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wanli merit against Shaanxi tribal raiders was ordered to follow the Chenghua rule: a company commander with five hundred men needed thirty heads from his unit, or sixty with a thousand; a platoon leader needed ten or thirty respectively—all earning one rank, to a ceiling of three.

sentences.zh: 南方蠻賊，宣德九年例，三級以上及斬獲首賊，俱升一秩，餘加賞。

translations.literal: Southern barbarian bandits—ninth year of Xuande precedent: three heads and above, or beheading and capturing bandit chiefs, all promoted one rank, remainder in additional reward.
translations.idiomatic: Against southern tribal rebels, the Xuande nine precedent granted one rank for three heads or for capturing a bandit chief; further merit brought additional reward.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年，定軍官部下斬百級者升署一秩，三百級者實授一秩，四百級者升一秩，餘功加賞。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year of Zhende—fixed: officers whose subordinates behead a hundred heads receive one acting rank; three hundred heads, one substantive rank; four hundred heads, one rank promotion; remaining merit in additional reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde it was fixed that an officer whose men accounted for a hundred heads received one acting rank; three hundred brought substantive rank; four hundred, a full promotion; any surplus was paid in silver.

sentences.zh: 倭賊，嘉靖三十五年定：「斬倭首賊一級，升實授三秩，不願者賞銀百五十兩。

translations.literal: Japanese pirates—fixed in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing: "Beheading one Japanese pirate chief—promoted three substantive ranks; those unwilling receive one hundred fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: For the wokou, the Jiajing thirty-five rule held: "Beheading a pirate chieftain earned three substantive ranks, or one hundred fifty taels for those who declined promotion.

sentences.zh: 從賊一級，授一秩。

translations.literal: One bandit follower head—one substantive rank.
translations.idiomatic: One ordinary pirate follower earned one substantive rank.

sentences.zh: 漢人脅從一級，署一秩。

translations.literal: One Han Chinese coerced follower head—one acting rank.
translations.idiomatic: One head from a Han Chinese pressed into service earned one acting rank.

sentences.zh: 陣亡者，本軍及子實授一秩。

translations.literal: Those killed in battle—the soldier's unit and his son each receive one substantive rank.
translations.idiomatic: A man killed in action earned one substantive rank for his unit and one for his son.

sentences.zh: 海洋遇賊有功，均以奇功論。」

translations.literal: Merit in encountering pirates at sea is all classified as extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Any merit won in an encounter with pirates at sea was counted as extraordinary merit.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十二年更定，視舊例少變，以賊眾及船之多寡，為功賞之差。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Wanli it was revised, slightly varying from the old precedent—the difference in merit rewards depending on number of bandits and ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Wanli the scale was revised, with slight changes from the old rule: rewards now varied according to the number of pirates and ships involved.

sentences.zh: 復定海洋徵戰，無論倭寇、海賊，勘是奇功，與世襲。

translations.literal: It was again fixed that maritime campaigns, whether against Japanese pirates or sea bandits, verified as extraordinary merit would receive hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: It was further decreed that in naval campaigns, whether against wokou or ordinary sea robbers, merit verified as extraordinary would carry hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 雲南夷賊，擒斬功次視倭功。

translations.literal: Yunnan barbarian bandits—merit for capture and beheading ranked below Japanese pirate merit.
translations.idiomatic: Merit against Yunnan tribal rebels ranked below that against the wokou.

sentences.zh: 內地反賊，成化十四年例，六級升一秩，至三秩止，幼男婦女及十九級以上與不及數者給賞。

translations.literal: Internal rebels—Chenghua fourteenth year precedent: six heads for one rank, up to three ranks; boys, women, and nineteen heads and above or failing to reach number receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: Against internal rebels, the Chenghua fourteen rule granted one rank for six heads, to a maximum of three; heads from boys and women, or totals of nineteen or more, or short of the quota, were paid in cash.

sentences.zh: 正德七年，定流賊例：「名賊一級，授一秩，世襲，為從者給賞。

translations.literal: Seventh year of Zhende—fixed bandit precedent: "One noted bandit head—one substantive rank, hereditary; followers receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengde seven bandit rule held: "The head of a notorious rebel earned one substantive hereditary rank; accomplices received cash.

sentences.zh: 次賊一級，署一秩。

translations.literal: One secondary bandit head—one acting rank.
translations.idiomatic: The head of a lesser rebel earned one acting rank.

sentences.zh: 從賊三級及陣亡者，俱授一秩，世襲。

translations.literal: Three follower bandit heads, and those killed in battle—all receive one substantive rank, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Three heads from ordinary bandits, or death in battle, each earned one substantive hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 重傷回營死者，署一秩。」

translations.literal: Those who die after being severely wounded and returning to camp—one acting rank.
translations.idiomatic: A man who returned to camp mortally wounded and died there received one acting rank.

sentences.zh: 又以割耳多寡論功，最多者至升二秩，世襲。

translations.literal: Also merit was judged by the number of severed ears; the highest could rise two ranks, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was also measured by severed ears; the highest award reached two hereditary ranks.

sentences.zh: 先是，五年寧夏功，後嘉靖元年江西功，俱視流賊例。

translations.literal: Earlier, fifth year Ningxia merit, and later first year of Jiajing Jiangxi merit, both followed the bandit precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, rewards for the Ningxia campaign of the fifth year, and later for Jiangxi in the first year of Jiajing, had both followed the bandit precedent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，購闖、獻以萬金，爵封侯，餘賊有差，以賊勢重，變常格也。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period, Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong were purchased for ten thousand gold, ennobled as marquises; other bandits at varying rates—because bandit strength was great, normal standards were altered.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era a price of ten thousand gold was put on Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong, with ennoblement as marquis; lesser rebels carried lower bounties—a departure from ordinary practice, forced by the rebels' overwhelming strength.

sentences.zh: 其俘獲人畜、器械，成化例，俱給所獲者。

translations.literal: Captured people, livestock, and weapons—Chenghua precedent, all given to the capturers.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners, livestock, and weapons taken in battle, under the Chenghua rule, went to those who captured them.

sentences.zh: 其論功升秩，成化十四年例，軍士升一秩為小旗，舍人升一秩給冠帶，以上類推。

translations.literal: Promotion by merit—Chenghua fourteenth year precedent: soldiers promoted one rank become corporals; bodyguards promoted one rank receive cap and belt; higher ranks follow by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: For promotion by merit, the Chenghua fourteen rule held that a common soldier rising one rank became a corporal; a garrison runner received cap and belt; higher ranks advanced by the same logic.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十三年定，都督等官無階可升者，所應襲男廕冠帶。

translations.literal: Fixed in the forty-third year of Jiajing: when regional commanders and the like have no rank left to which to ascend, the male heir due to inherit receives ennobled cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Jiajing it was fixed that when a regional commander had no further rank to which he could rise, the son due to inherit his post received an ennobled cap and belt instead.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十三年定，都指揮使升秩者，不授都督，賞銀五十兩，升俸者半之。

translations.literal: Fixed in the thirteenth year of Wanli: regional commanders promoted in rank do not receive the title of Commissioner-in-Chief—fifty taels reward; half that if only salary increase.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Wanli it was decreed that a regional commander promoted beyond his grade did not receive the title of Commissioner-in-Chief but fifty taels of silver—or half that if he took only a salary increase.

sentences.zh: 其有司民兵，隆慶六年定，視軍人例。

translations.literal: Militia under local officials—fixed in the sixth year of Longqing—follow the soldier precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Militia levied by civil officials, fixed in the sixth year of Longqing, were rewarded under the same rules as regular soldiers.

sentences.zh: 自洪、宣以後，賞格皆以斬級多少豫定。

translations.literal: From Hongwu and Xuande onward, reward scales were all predetermined by number of heads beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: From the Hongwu and Xuande reigns onward, reward tables were set in advance according to the number of heads taken.

sentences.zh: 條例漸多，幸弊日啟。

translations.literal: Regulations gradually multiplied, and abuses arose daily.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes multiplied year by year, and abuses arose daily with them.

sentences.zh: 正德間，副使胡世寧言：「兩軍格鬥，手眼瞬息，不得差池，何暇割級？

translations.literal: During Zhengde, Vice Commissioner Hu Shining said: "When two armies grapple, hand and eye in an instant—one cannot afford the slightest lapse; who has leisure to sever heads?
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign Vice Commissioner Hu Shining argued: "When two armies clash, hand and eye must move in an instant—not a moment's slack is permitted. Who has time to hack off heads?

sentences.zh: 其獲級者或殺已降，或殺良民，或偶得單行之賊、被掠逃出之人，非真功也。

translations.literal: Those who obtain heads may have killed already surrendered men, or killed innocent civilians, or happened upon a lone bandit or someone stolen and escaped—not true merit.
translations.idiomatic: Men who brought in heads might have slaughtered prisoners, murdered civilians, or stumbled on a lone straggler or a peasant seized and then released by the enemy—none of which was genuine merit.

sentences.zh: 宜選強明剛正之員，為紀功官，痛懲此弊。」

translations.literal: Strong, perceptive, upright officials should be chosen as merit-recording officers to severely punish this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Capable, clear-sighted, and upright officers should be appointed as merit auditors to root out this fraud.

sentences.zh: 時弗能行。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing came of the proposal.

sentences.zh: 故事，鎮守官奏帶，例止五名。

translations.literal: By established practice, garrison commanders submitting accompanying personnel lists were limited to five names.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, a garrison commander reporting men to be rewarded alongside him might name at most five.

sentences.zh: 後領兵官所奏有至三四百名者，不在斬馘之列，別立名目，曰運送神槍，曰齎執旗牌，曰衝鋒破敵，曰三次當先，曰軍前效勞。

translations.literal: Later, field commanders submitting lists reached as many as three or four hundred, not in the category of beheaded heads but given separate designations: transporting divine muskets, carrying flags and plaques, charging to break the enemy, being foremost three times, serving meritoriously before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Later, commanders in the field submitted rolls of three or four hundred names—men who had taken no heads at all but were rewarded under new categories: transporting divine muskets, bearing flags and insignia, charging to break the enemy, leading the assault three times, and serving with distinction at the front.

sentences.zh: 冒濫之弊，至斯極已。

translations.literal: The evil of reckless excess had reached this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The abuse of over-provisioning had reached its zenith.

sentences.zh: 古所謂砲，皆以機發石。

translations.literal: What the ancients called cannon all used mechanisms to hurl stones.
translations.idiomatic: The cannon of antiquity were all stone-throwing engines worked by mechanical trigger.

sentences.zh: 元初得西域砲，攻金蔡州城，始用火。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, having obtained Western Region cannon, they attacked the Jin city of Caizhou and first used fire.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuan, after capturing cannon from the Western Regions, they besieged Caizhou of Jin and for the first time brought gunpowder to bear.

sentences.zh: 然造法不傳，後亦罕用。

translations.literal: Yet the method of manufacture was not transmitted, and afterward it was rarely used.
translations.idiomatic: The craft was never handed down, and in later times such weapons saw little service.

sentences.zh: 至明成祖平交阯，得神機槍砲法，特置神機營肄習。

translations.literal: When the Ming Chengzu pacified Jiaozhi, he obtained the methods of the divine-engine gun and cannon and specially established the Divine Engine Corps for drill.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Yongle Emperor subdued Jiaozhi did the court acquire the art of muskets and cannon, whereupon it founded the Shenji Camp expressly to train men in their use.

sentences.zh: 制用生、熟赤銅相間，其用鐵者，建鐵柔為最，西鐵次之。

translations.literal: In manufacture, raw and wrought red copper were used in alternation; where iron was used, soft Jian iron was best, and Western iron next.
translations.idiomatic: They were cast from layers of raw and refined copper; when iron was employed, pliant Jian iron ranked first and Western iron second.

sentences.zh: 大小不等，大者發用車，次及小者用架、用樁、用託。

translations.literal: Their sizes were unequal: the largest were fired from carts; those somewhat smaller used frames, stakes, or rests.
translations.idiomatic: They varied in size—the great pieces were served from wagons, the lesser from frames, posts, or cradles.

sentences.zh: 大利於守，小利於戰。

translations.literal: They greatly favored defense and little favored battle.
translations.idiomatic: They served defense far better than open field combat.

sentences.zh: 隨宜而用，為行軍要器。

translations.literal: Used as circumstances required, they were essential equipment on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Employed as occasion demanded, they became indispensable to marching armies.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年，詔自開平至懷來、宣府、萬全、興和諸山頂，皆置五砲架。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle, an edict ordered five-cannon frames placed on every mountaintop from Kaiping to Huailai, Xuanfu, Wanquan, and Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 10, the throne commanded that five-gun platforms be erected on the peaks from Kaiping through Huailai, Xuanfu, Wanquan, and Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 二十年，從張輔請，增置於山西大同、天城、陽和、朔州等衛以禦敵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, at Zhang Fu's request, more were added at the garrisons of Datong, Tiancheng, Yanghe, and Shuozhou in Shanxi to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years on, at Zhang Fu's urging, additional pieces were posted to the Shanxi garrisons of Datong, Tiancheng, Yanghe, and Shuozhou for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 然利器不可示人，朝廷亦慎惜之。

translations.literal: Yet sharp weapons must not be shown to others, and the court also guarded them with care.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a keen blade is not lightly displayed, and the court treated these arms with equal caution.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖八年，始從右都御史汪鋐言，造佛郎機砲，謂之大將軍，發諸邊鎮。

translations.literal: Not until the eighth year of Jiajing did the court, following the memorial of the Right Censor-in-chief Wang Hong, manufacture Frankish cannon, calling them Great Generals, and issue them to the border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Jiajing 8, on the advice of Wang Hong, Right Censor-in-chief, did the court begin casting Frankish cannon—styled Great Generals—and distributing them to the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 佛郎機者，國名也。

translations.literal: Frankish is the name of a country.
translations.idiomatic: Folangji was the name of a foreign realm.

sentences.zh: 正德末，其國舶至廣東。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengde, ships of that country reached Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengde reign, its vessels appeared off Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 白沙巡檢何儒得其制，以銅為之。

translations.literal: He Ru, patrol inspector of Baisha, obtained its design and made it in copper.
translations.idiomatic: He Ru, the Baisha patrol inspector, secured the design and reproduced it in bronze.

sentences.zh: 長五六尺，大者重千餘斤，小者百五十斤，巨腹長頸，腹有修孔。

translations.literal: It was five or six feet long; the large weighed more than a thousand jin and the small one hundred fifty jin; it had a great belly and long neck, with loading holes in the belly.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six feet in length, the largest weighed over a thousand jin and the smallest a hundred and fifty; its body swelled and its neck ran long, pierced with touch-holes along the chamber.

sentences.zh: 以子銃五枚，貯藥置腹中，發及百餘丈，最利水戰。

translations.literal: With five chambered barrels, powder was stored in the belly; its range exceeded a hundred zhang, and it was best suited to river and sea fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Five nested barrels held the charge within the breech; it could reach beyond a hundred zhang and proved deadliest in naval warfare.

sentences.zh: 駕以蜈蚣船，所擊輒糜碎。

translations.literal: Mounted on centipede boats, whatever they struck was shattered to fragments.
translations.idiomatic: Set aboard centipede warships, a single hit reduced its target to splinters.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，總督軍務翁萬達奏所造火器。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Weng Wanda, Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs, memorialized on the fire weapons he had made.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, Weng Wanda, overseer of military affairs, submitted a report on the fire-arms he had devised.

sentences.zh: 兵部試之，言：「三出連珠、百出先鋒、鐵捧雷飛，俱便用。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War tested them and said: 'Three-Shot Linked Pearls, Hundred-Shot Vanguard, and Iron Club Thunderflight are all convenient to use.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War tested them and declared: 'The Three-Shot Linked Pearls, the Hundred-Shot Vanguard, and the Iron Club Thunderflight are all serviceable weapons.

sentences.zh: 母子火獸、布地雷砲，止可夜劫營。」

translations.literal: The Mother-and-Son Fire Beast and the Cloth-Spread Land-Mine Cannon are fit only for night raids on camps.
translations.idiomatic: The Mother-and-Son Fire Beast and the Cloth-Spread Land-Mine Cannon may be used only in nocturnal assaults on enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 御史張鐸亦進十眼銅砲，大彈發及七百步，小彈百步；

translations.literal: The censor Zhang Duo also presented a ten-eyed copper cannon: large shot reached seven hundred paces and small shot a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Duo likewise offered a ten-barreled bronze cannon whose great shot carried seven hundred paces and whose small shot a hundred.

sentences.zh: 四眼鐵槍，彈四百步。

translations.literal: The four-eyed iron gun shot four hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: A four-barreled iron gun reached four hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 詔工部造。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Works to manufacture them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commanded the Ministry of Works to cast them.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，通判華光大奏其父所制神異火器，命下兵部。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, the assistant prefect Hua Guangda memorialized the wondrous fire weapons his father had made, and the order was sent down to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, Assistant Prefect Hua Guangda presented his father's marvelous fire-arms, and the matter was referred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 其後，大西洋船至，復得巨砲，曰紅夷。

translations.literal: Afterward, ships from the Great Atlantic arrived, and giant cannon were obtained again, called Red Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Later, vessels from the Great Western Ocean came, bringing once more enormous guns known as Red Barbarian cannon.

sentences.zh: 長二丈餘，重者至三千斤，能洞裂石城，震數十里。

translations.literal: They were more than two zhang long; the heaviest reached three thousand jin and could pierce and split stone walls, shaking the ground for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Over two zhang in length and weighing up to three thousand jin, they could breach stone ramparts and make the earth tremble for tens of li.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，錫以大將軍號，遣官祀之。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period, one was honored with the title Great General, and officials were sent to offer sacrifice to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign, one such piece was granted the rank of Great General, and officers were dispatched to pay it ritual homage.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，大學士徐光啟請令西洋人製造，發各鎮。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period, Grand Secretary Xu Guangqi requested that Westerners be ordered to manufacture them and that they be issued to the garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen, Grand Secretary Xu Guangqi urged that Western artisans be commissioned to build them and that the pieces be distributed to the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 然將帥多不得人，城守不固，有委而去之者。

translations.literal: Yet commanders often lacked worthy men, city defenses were not firm, and some abandoned their posts and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yet too many posts went to unworthy officers; garrisons stood weak, and some defenders simply threw down their arms and fled.

sentences.zh: 及流寇犯闕，三大營兵不戰而潰，槍砲皆為賊有，反用以攻城。

translations.literal: When the roving bandits assaulted the capital, the soldiers of the three great camps collapsed without fighting, and guns and cannon all fell to the rebels, who turned them against the cities.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel hosts reached the capital, the three great encampments broke without a fight; muskets and cannon passed into bandit hands and were turned back upon the walled cities.

sentences.zh: 城上亦發砲擊賊。

translations.literal: On the walls, cannon were also fired to strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: From the ramparts, defenders answered with cannon fire of their own.

sentences.zh: 時中官已多異志，皆空器貯藥，取聲震而已。

translations.literal: By then many eunuchs already harbored other designs; they emptied the weapons and kept only stored powder, seeking nothing but the thunder of the blast.
translations.idiomatic: By then many eunuchs had turned disloyal; they stripped the guns of shot and kept powder only, contenting themselves with the roar of empty thunder.

sentences.zh: 明置兵仗、軍器二局，分造火器。

translations.literal: The Ming established two offices, the Military Equipment Bureau and the Military Implements Bureau, to manufacture fire weapons separately.
