translations.idiomatic: The Ming set up two workshops—the Military Equipment Bureau and the Military Implements Bureau—each charged with producing fire-arms.

sentences.zh: 號將軍者自大至五。

translations.literal: Those styled General ranged from the First to the Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Pieces bearing the title General ran from the First Rank down to the Fifth.

sentences.zh: 又有奪門將軍大小二樣、神機砲、襄陽砲、盞口砲、碗口砲、旋風砲、流星砲、虎尾砲、石榴砲、龍虎砲、毒火飛砲、連珠佛郎機砲、信砲、神砲、砲裏砲、十眼銅砲、三出連珠砲、百出先鋒砲、鐵捧雷飛砲、火獸布地雷砲、碗口銅鐵銃、手把銅鐵銃、神銃、斬馬銃、一窩鋒神機箭銃、大中小佛郎機銅銃、佛郎機鐵銃、木廂銅銃、筋繳樺皮鐵銃、無敵手銃、鳥嘴銃、七眼銅銃、千里銃、四眼鐵槍、各號雙頭鐵槍、夾把鐵手槍、快槍以及火車、火傘、九龍筒之屬，凡數十種。

translations.literal: There were also Gate-Storming Generals in large and small patterns, divine-engine cannon, Xiangyang cannon, bowl-mouth cannon, whirlwind cannon, meteor cannon, tiger-tail cannon, pomegranate cannon, dragon-and-tiger cannon, poison-fire flying cannon, linked-pearl Frankish cannon, signal cannon, divine cannon, cannon-within-cannon, ten-eyed copper cannon, three-shot linked-pearl cannon, hundred-shot vanguard cannon, iron-club thunderflight cannon, fire-beast cloth land-mine cannon, bowl-mouth copper-and-iron muskets, hand-held copper-and-iron muskets, divine muskets, horse-slaying muskets, one-nest sharp divine-engine arrow muskets, large, medium, and small Frankish muskets, Frankish iron muskets, wooden-cased copper muskets, sinew-lacquered birch-bark iron muskets, Invincible Hand muskets, bird-beak muskets, seven-eyed copper muskets, Thousand-Li muskets, four-eyed iron guns, double-headed iron guns of every grade, paired-grip iron hand guns, fast guns, and such things as fire carts, fire umbrellas, and nine-dragon tubes—several dozen kinds in all.
translations.idiomatic: The inventory further included Gate-Storming Generals in two sizes; Shenji, Xiangyang, bowl-mouth, whirlwind, meteor, tiger-tail, pomegranate, dragon-and-tiger, poison-fire flying, linked-pearl Frankish, signal, divine, and nested cannon; ten-eyed bronze guns; three-shot pearls, hundred-shot vanguards, iron-club thunderflights, and fire-beast land-mines; bowl-mouth, hand-held, divine, horse-slaying, one-nest arrow, large and small Frankish, Frankish iron, wooden-cased, lacquered-bark, Invincible Hand, bird-beak, seven-eyed, Thousand-Li, and four-eyed iron pieces; double-headed and paired-grip hand guns; fast guns; and fire carts, fire umbrellas, and nine-dragon tubes—several score types in all.

sentences.zh: 正德、嘉靖間造最多。

translations.literal: Most were made between the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Production peaked in the Zhengde and Jiajing eras.

sentences.zh: 又各邊自造，自正統十四年四川始。

translations.literal: Each frontier also made its own; this began in Sichuan in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: The border commands likewise cast their own arms—a practice that began in Sichuan in Zhengtong 14.

sentences.zh: 其他刀牌、弓箭、槍弩、狼筅、蒺藜、甲冑、戰襖，在內有兵仗、軍器、針工、鞍轡諸局，屬內庫，掌於中官，在外有盔甲廠，屬兵部，掌以郎官。

translations.literal: Other items—swords and shields, bows and arrows, spears and crossbows, wolf-brushes, caltrops, armor, and battle jackets—were made within by the Military Equipment, Military Implements, Needlework, and Harness bureaus under the Inner Treasury, managed by eunuchs; without, by the Armor Factory under the Ministry of War, managed by departmental officials.
translations.idiomatic: Swords, shields, bows, arrows, spears, crossbows, wolf-brushes, caltrops, armor, and padded battle coats were forged within by the Military Equipment, Military Implements, Needlework, and Harness offices of the Inner Treasury under eunuch control, and without by the Armor Factory of the Ministry of War under its departmental officers.

sentences.zh: 京省諸司衛所，又俱有雜造局。

translations.literal: Offices, garrisons, and posts in the capital and provinces all likewise had miscellaneous manufacture bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Every yamen, guard, and post in the capital and provinces maintained its own general workshop as well.

sentences.zh: 軍資器械名目繁夥，不具載，惟火器前代所少，故特詳焉。

translations.literal: The names of military stores and equipment were numerous and complex and are not fully recorded here; only fire weapons, which previous dynasties had in small number, are treated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The catalogue of arms and materiel runs too long to set down in full; fire weapons alone, scarce in earlier ages, are here described at length.

sentences.zh: 中原用車戰，而東南利舟楫，二者於兵事為最要。

translations.literal: The Central Plains favored chariot warfare, while the southeast favored boats and oars; of military affairs these two were most essential.
translations.idiomatic: In the heartland, war rested on chariots; along the southeastern coast, on ships—each the keystone of its region's way of war.

sentences.zh: 自騎兵起，車制漸廢。

translations.literal: Once cavalry arose, the chariot system was gradually abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: With the rise of mounted warfare, the chariot gradually fell from use.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年，造獨轅車，北平、山東千輛，山西、河南八百輛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu, single-pole chariots were made: one thousand for Beiping and Shandong, eight hundred for Shanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 5, single-shaft wagons were built—a thousand for Beiping and Shandong, eight hundred for Shanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年北征，用武剛車三萬輛，皆惟以供饋運。

translations.literal: On the northern expedition of the eighth year of Yongle, thirty thousand Wugang chariots were used, all solely to carry supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle's northern campaign of the eighth year employed thirty thousand Wugang wagons, every one devoted to transport.

sentences.zh: 至正統十二年，始從總兵官硃冕議，用火車備戰。

translations.literal: Not until the twelfth year of Zhengtong did the court, following the proposal of the commander-in-chief Zhu Mian, adopt fire chariots for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Zhengtong 12, on Commander Zhu Mian's recommendation, were fire-wagons introduced for combat.

sentences.zh: 自是言車戰者相繼。

translations.literal: From this time advocates of chariot warfare followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, memorials urging chariot warfare came in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 十四年，給事中李侃請以ＣＡ車千輛，鐵索聯絡，騎卒處中，每車翼以刀牌手五人，賊犯陣，刀牌手擊之，賊退則開索縱騎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the supervising secretary Li Kan requested a thousand ram chariots linked by iron chains, with cavalry stationed in the center; each chariot would be flanked by five sword-and-shield men—when the enemy struck the formation the sword-and-shield men would beat them back, and when the enemy withdrew the chains would be opened to release the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Supervising Secretary Li Kan proposed a thousand ram chariots bound with iron chains, cavalry held in the center, and five sword-and-shield fighters on either flank of each wagon—blades to repel a charge, chains parted to let the horsemen pursue a retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝命造成祭而後用。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that they be completed and sacrificial rites performed before use.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded that the vehicles be finished and consecrated before they saw service.

sentences.zh: 下車式於邊境，用七馬駕。

translations.literal: The chariot pattern was sent to the frontier, to be drawn by seven horses.
translations.idiomatic: The design was dispatched to the border commands, each team to be pulled by seven horses.

sentences.zh: 寧夏多溝壑，總兵官張泰請用獨馬小車，時以為便。

translations.literal: Ningxia had many ravines and gullies; the commander Zhang Tai requested single-horse small carts, which at the time were considered convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia's broken terrain prompted Commander Zhang Tai to ask for one-horse light carts, then judged the handiest option.

sentences.zh: 箭工週四章言，神機槍一發難繼，請以車載槍二十，箭六百，車首置五槍架，一人推，二人扶，一人執爨。

translations.literal: The bowyer Zhou Sizhang said that once a divine-engine gun was fired it was hard to reload in succession, and requested a cart carrying twenty guns and six hundred arrows, with five gun mounts at the front—one man to push, two to steady, and one to tend the brazier.
translations.idiomatic: Bowyer Zhou Sizhang argued that the Shenji musket could not be fired in quick succession and proposed a cart bearing twenty pieces and six hundred bolts, five gun-stands on the bow, one man pushing, two steadying, and one tending the match.

sentences.zh: 試可，乃造。

translations.literal: The trial proved satisfactory, and they were then manufactured.
translations.idiomatic: Trials satisfied the court, and construction followed.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，定襄伯郭登請仿古制為偏箱車。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, the Earl of Dingxiang, Guo Deng, requested that flank-box chariots be made according to the ancient pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1, Dingxiang Earl Guo Deng urged a return to the old flank-box chariot.

sentences.zh: 轅長丈三尺，闊九尺，高七尺五寸，箱用薄板，置銃。

translations.literal: The pole was one zhang and three feet long, nine feet wide, and seven feet five inches high; the box used thin boards and held muskets.
translations.idiomatic: The shaft measured one zhang three feet; the body, nine feet across and seven feet five inches high, was panelled in thin wood and fitted with muskets.

sentences.zh: 出則左右相連，前後相接，鉤環牽互。

translations.literal: When deployed, they linked left and right and joined front and back, hooks and rings interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the field they chained flank to flank and end to end, hooks and rings binding the line.

sentences.zh: 車載衣糧、器械並鹿角二。

translations.literal: Each chariot carried clothing, grain, equipment, and two chevaux-de-frise.
translations.idiomatic: Each wagon bore rations, gear, and a pair of abatis.

sentences.zh: 屯處，十五步外設為籓。

translations.literal: When encamped, a barrier was set fifteen paces out.
translations.idiomatic: In camp, a palisade was thrown up fifteen paces beyond the wagons.

sentences.zh: 每車槍砲、弓弩、刀牌甲士共十人，無事輪番推輓。

translations.literal: Each chariot had ten men for guns, cannon, bows, crossbows, swords, shields, and armor; in quiet times they took turns pushing and hauling.
translations.idiomatic: Ten men crewed each vehicle—gunners, archers, crossbowmen, and sword-and-shield fighters—who rotated the work of hauling when idle.

sentences.zh: 外以長車二十，載大小將軍銃，每方五輛，轉輸樵採，皆在圍中。

translations.literal: Outside, twenty long chariots carried large and small General muskets, five to each side, for hauling wood and foraging, all kept within the perimeter.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty supply wagons ringed the formation, five to a face, bearing Great General pieces of every size for wood-gathering and forage, all kept inside the enclosure.

sentences.zh: 又以四輪車一，列五色旗，視敵指揮。

translations.literal: There was also one four-wheeled chariot bearing five-colored flags to direct movements according to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: A four-wheeled command car flying five-colored pennants directed the array against the foe.

sentences.zh: 廷議此可以守，難於攻戰，命登酌行。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that this could defend but was hard to use in attack; the emperor ordered Deng to implement it as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged the scheme sound for defense but ill-suited to the attack and bade Guo Deng carry it out at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 蘭州守備李進請造獨輪小車，上施皮屋，前用木板，畫獸面，鑿口，置碗口銃四，槍四，神機箭十四，樹旗一。

translations.literal: Li Jin, garrison commander of Lanzhou, requested the making of single-wheeled small carts with leather shelters on top, wooden boards in front painted with beast faces and pierced with mouths, holding four bowl-mouth cannon, four spears, fourteen divine-engine arrows, and one flag.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou Garrison Commander Li Jin proposed a one-wheeled cart capped with a leather awning, its prow boarded and painted with snarling beasts, muzzles cut through to mount four bowl-mouth guns, four spears, fourteen Shenji bolts, and a banner.

sentences.zh: 行為陣，止為營。

translations.literal: In motion it formed a battle line; at rest it formed a camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the march it became a fighting line; halted, a fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 二年，吏部郎中李賢請造戰車，長丈五尺，高六尺四寸，四圍箱板，穴孔置銃，上闢小窗，每車前後佔地五步。

translations.literal: In the second year, Li Xian, director in the Ministry of Personnel, requested the making of war chariots one zhang and five feet long and six feet four inches high, with box boards on all four sides, holes for muskets, and small windows opened above; each chariot front and rear occupied five paces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Ministry of Personnel Director Li Xian called for war wagons one zhang five feet long and six feet four inches high, boarded on every side with gun-ports and narrow windows aloft, each vehicle claiming ten paces fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 以千輛計，四方可十六里，芻糧、器械輜重鹹取給焉。

translations.literal: Counting by the thousand chariots, the four sides could cover sixteen li; fodder, grain, equipment, and baggage would all be drawn from within.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand such wagons, arrayed square, would enclose sixteen li; fodder, arms, and baggage would all be drawn from the interior.

sentences.zh: 帝令亟行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered immediate implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded that the plan be executed at once.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，從郭登言，制軍隊小車。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua, following Guo Deng's proposal, small chariots for army units were made.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 2 saw the adoption of Guo Deng's design for company-scale light wagons.

sentences.zh: 每隊六輛，輛九人，二人挽，七人番代，車前置牌畫猊首，遠望若城壘然。

translations.literal: Each squad had six chariots and nine men per chariot—two to haul and seven to relieve in rotation; a shield painted with a lion's head was set before each chariot, so that from afar it looked like a city rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Each squad fielded six wagons crewed by nine men apiece—two pulling, seven relieving in turn—with a prow-shield painted in a lion's likeness so that, at a distance, the line resembled a wall.

sentences.zh: 八年，甯都諸生何京上御敵車式，上施鐵網，網穴發槍弩，行則斂之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, He Jing, a student of Ningdu, presented a design for an enemy-repelling chariot with an iron net on top; guns and crossbows fired through holes in the net, which was folded in when moving.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Ningdu scholar He Jing submitted plans for a counter-assault wagon topped with an iron mesh; muskets and crossbows spoke through its apertures, the net furled for the march.

sentences.zh: 五十車為一隊，用士三百七十五人。

translations.literal: Fifty chariots formed one squad, using three hundred seventy-five soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty wagons made a company, manned by three hundred seventy-five troops.

sentences.zh: 十二年，左都御史李賓請造偏箱車，與鹿角參用。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Left Censor-in-chief Li Bin requested the making of flank-box chariots to be used together with chevaux-de-frise.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Left Censor-in-chief Li Bin urged flank-box chariots to be deployed alongside abatis.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書項忠請驗閱，以登高涉險不便，已之。

translations.literal: The Minister of War Xiang Zhong requested inspection and review; because climbing heights and crossing difficult ground was inconvenient, the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Xiang Zhong ordered a trial, found the wagons useless on steep ground, and set the project aside.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從甘肅總兵官王璽奏，造雷火車，中立樞軸，旋轉發砲。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, following the memorial of Wang Xi, commander-in-chief of Gansu, thunder-fire chariots were made with a central pivot shaft to rotate and fire cannon.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on Gansu Commander Wang Xi's petition, thunder-fire wagons were built with a central axle to swivel and discharge their guns.

sentences.zh: 二十年，宣大總督餘子俊以車五百輛為一軍，每輛卒十人，車隙補以鹿角。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Yu Zijun, grand coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong, made five hundred chariots one army, with ten soldiers per chariot and gaps filled with chevaux-de-frise.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Xuan-Datong Grand Coordinator Yu Zijun formed an army of five hundred wagons, ten men to each, the intervals studded with abatis.

sentences.zh: 既成，而遲重不可用，時人謂之鷓鴣軍。

translations.literal: Once completed they proved slow and heavy and unusable; people of the time called them the Partridge Army.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the train proved too lumbering for battle; contemporaries mocked it as the Partridge Host.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年，陝西總制秦紘請用只輪車，名曰全勝，長丈四尺，上下共六人，可沖敵陣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, Qin Gang, grand coordinator of Shaanxi, requested the use of single-wheel chariots called Total Victory, one zhang and four feet long, with six men above and below, able to charge enemy formations.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 15 brought Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Qin Geng's single-wheeled Total Victory cart—one zhang four feet long, six fighters aboard, built to smash through enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 十六年，閑住知府範吉獻先鋒霹靂車。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Fan Ji, a prefect on leave, presented the Vanguard Thunderclap chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Prefect Fan Ji, then at leisure, offered his Vanguard Thunderclap wagon.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年，南京給事中王希文請仿郭固、韓琦之制，造車，前銳後方，上置七槍，為櫓三層，各置九牛神弩，傍翼以卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing, Wang Xiwen, supervising secretary of Nanjing, requested chariots modeled on the designs of Guo Gu and Han Qi—sharp in front and square behind, with seven guns mounted above, built as a three-tier ram, each tier fitted with a nine-ox divine crossbow, and flanked by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 11 saw Nanjing Supervising Secretary Wang Xiwen propose wagons after the models of Guo Gu and Han Qi—wedge-nosed and square-sterned, seven guns on the deck, a triple-tiered battering tower each mounting a nine-ox siege bow, infantry on the flanks.

sentences.zh: 行載甲兵，止為營陣。

translations.literal: On the march they carried armored troops; at rest they served as camp formations.
translations.idiomatic: They would haul armored infantry on campaign and serve as fortified camps at halt.

sentences.zh: 下邊鎮酌行。

translations.literal: The design was sent to the border garrisons to implement as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The plans were forwarded to the frontier commands for such use as local conditions allowed.

sentences.zh: 十五年，總制劉天和復言全勝車之便，而稍為損益，用四人推輓，所載火器、弓弩、刀牌以百五十斤為準。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Grand Coordinator Liu Tianhe again spoke of the convenience of the Total Victory chariot, with slight modifications: four men to push and haul, and fire weapons, bows, crossbows, swords, and shields loaded to a standard of one hundred fifty jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Grand Coordinator Liu Tianhe renewed praise for the Total Victory cart with modest revisions—four men to haul it, its armament of guns, bows, blades, and shields reckoned at a hundred and fifty jin.

sentences.zh: 箱前畫狻猊，旁列虎盾以護騎士。

translations.literal: On the front of the box a suanni was painted, and tiger shields were ranged on the sides to protect horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: A suanni was painted on the prow, tiger shields lined the flanks to shelter the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 命從其制。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that his design be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his specifications.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，有司奏準，京營教演兵車，共四千輛，每輛步卒五人，神槍、夾靶槍各二。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, officials memorialized for approval to drill war chariots in the capital garrison—four thousand in all, five infantrymen per chariot, each with two divine guns and two paired-target spears.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, the court authorized four thousand drill wagons for the capital encampments—five foot soldiers apiece, each crew bearing two Shenji pieces and two paired-target spears.

sentences.zh: 自正統以來，言車戰者如此，然未嘗一當敵。

translations.literal: From Zhengtong onward, advocates of chariot warfare were as described above, yet they never once met the enemy in battle.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhengtong reign on, chariot schemes multiplied as here set forth—yet not one ever stood a real fight.

sentences.zh: 至隆慶中，戚繼光守薊門，奏練兵車七營：以東西路副總兵及撫督標共四營，分駐建昌、遵化、石匣、密雲；

translations.literal: In the Longqing period, Qi Jiguang, defending Jimen, memorialized on drilling seven chariot camps: four camps under the east-and-west route vice commanders and the grand coordinator's banner, stationed at Jianchang, Zunhua, Shixia, and Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longqing, Qi Jiguang, holding Jimen, proposed seven chariot brigades—four under the eastern and western route lieutenant-generals and the governor's standard, posted at Jianchang, Zunhua, Shixia, and Miyun.

sentences.zh: 薊、遼總兵二營，駐三屯；

translations.literal: Two camps under the Ji and Liaodong commanders-in-chief were stationed at Santun.
translations.idiomatic: Two brigades under the Ji and Liaodong commanders garrisoned Santun.

sentences.zh: 昌平總兵一營，駐昌平。

translations.literal: One camp under the Changping commander-in-chief was stationed at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: One brigade under the Changping commander held Changping itself.

sentences.zh: 每營重車百五十有六，輕車加百，步兵四千，騎兵三千。

translations.literal: Each camp had one hundred fifty-six heavy chariots and one hundred light chariots in addition, four thousand infantry, and three thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Each brigade fielded a hundred fifty-six heavy wagons and a hundred light ones besides, four thousand foot and three thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 十二路二千里間，車騎相兼，可禦敵數萬。

translations.literal: Along twelve routes over two thousand li, chariots and cavalry combined could repel an enemy of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Spanning twelve lines and two thousand li, the combined chariot-and-horse force could stand against tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 穆宗韙之，命給造費。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor approved it and ordered funds provided for manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong assented and appropriated the cost of building them.

sentences.zh: 然特以遏衝突，施火器，亦未嘗以戰也。

translations.literal: Yet they were intended only to check charges and deploy fire weapons, and were likewise never used in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were meant chiefly to break enemy rushes and bring fire-arms to bear—and they, too, never saw battle.

sentences.zh: 是後，遼東巡撫魏學曾請設戰車營，仿偏箱之制，上設佛郎機二，下置雷飛砲、快槍六，每車步卒二十五人。

translations.literal: Afterward, Wei Xuezeng, governor of Liaodong, requested the establishment of a war-chariot camp modeled on the flank-box design, with two Frankish guns mounted above and six thunderflight cannon and fast guns below, twenty-five infantrymen per chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Liaodong Governor Wei Xuezeng asked for a chariot battalion on the flank-box pattern—two Frankish pieces on the roof, six thunderflight guns and fast muskets below, twenty-five foot soldiers per wagon.

sentences.zh: 萬曆末，經略熊廷弼請造雙輪戰車，每車火砲二，翼以十卒，皆持火槍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli, the frontier commissioner Xiong Tingbi requested the making of double-wheeled war chariots, each with two fire cannon and ten flanking soldiers, all bearing fire guns.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wanli, Frontier Commissioner Xiong Tingbi proposed two-wheeled fighting carts, each mounting two cannon and ten escorts armed with muskets.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，直隸巡按御史易應昌進戶部主事曹履吉所制鋼輪車、小沖車等式，以禦敵，皆罕得其用。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period, Yi Yingchang, touring censor of Zhili, presented designs by Cao Luji, director in the Ministry of Revenue, for steel-wheeled chariots, small ram chariots, and the like to repel the enemy; none found much use.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, Zhili Touring Censor Yi Yingchang submitted Revenue Director Cao Luji's designs for steel-wheeled wagons and light ram carts—none of which ever came to much.

sentences.zh: 大約邊地險阻，不利車戰。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the borderlands were rugged and unfavorable to chariot warfare.
translations.idiomatic: On the whole, the frontier's broken ground ill suited the chariot.

sentences.zh: 而舟楫之用，則東南所宜。

translations.literal: The use of boats and oars, however, was what the southeast required.
translations.idiomatic: Ships and oars, by contrast, were the arm the southeast demanded.

sentences.zh: 舟之制，江海各異。

translations.literal: The construction of boats differed between river and sea.
translations.idiomatic: River craft and seagoing vessels were built to different designs.

sentences.zh: 太祖於新江口設船四百。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor at Xinkou established four hundred ships.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor posted four hundred vessels at Xinkou.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，命福建都司造海船百三十七，又命江、楚、兩浙及鎮江諸府衛造海風船。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, he ordered the Fujian regional command to build one hundred thirty-seven sea ships, and further ordered the prefectures and guards of Jiang, Chu, the Two Zhe, and Zhenjiang to build sea wind ships.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, the court ordered the Fujian regional command to build a hundred thirty-seven seagoing vessels, and likewise charged the Jiang, Chu, Two-Zhe, and Zhenjiang prefectures and guards with building offshore sailing ships.

sentences.zh: 成化初，濟川衛楊渠獻《槳舟圖》，皆江舟也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Yang Qu of Jichuan Guard presented the "Diagram of Oar Boats"; all were river boats.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Chenghua, Yang Qu of Jichuan Guard submitted the Illustrated Oar-Craft—all designs for river vessels.

sentences.zh: 海舟以舟山之烏槽為首。

translations.literal: Among sea boats, the Wucao of Zhoushan ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among seagoing craft, the wucao of Zhoushan stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 福船耐風濤，且禦火。

translations.literal: Fujian ships endured wind and waves, and also resisted fire.
translations.idiomatic: Fukienese junks rode out wind and sea swells and could withstand fire as well.

sentences.zh: 浙之十裝標號軟風、蒼山，亦利追逐。

translations.literal: Zhejiang's ten-rig ships were labeled Ruofeng and Cangshan; they were also suited for pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Chekiang's ten-rig vessels, marked Ruofeng and Cangshan, were likewise nimble in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 廣東船，鐵慄木為之，視福船尤巨而堅。

translations.literal: Guangdong ships were made of iron chestnut wood; compared with Fujian ships they were yet greater and stouter.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese craft, built of iron chestnut timber, were larger and tougher still than Fukienese junks.

sentences.zh: 其利用者二，可發佛郎機，可擲火球。

translations.literal: Their uses were two: they could fire Portuguese cannon and cast fire balls.
translations.idiomatic: They had two chief strengths: they could mount falconets and launch fire-balls.

sentences.zh: 大福船亦然，能容百人。

translations.literal: Large Fujian ships were likewise so, able to hold a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The great Fukienese junk was the same, carrying as many as a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 底尖上闊，首昂尾高，柁樓三重，帆桅二，傍護以板，上設木女牆及砲牀。

translations.literal: Bottom pointed, upper broad; bow raised, stern high; steering tower three tiers; sails and masts two; flanked and protected with planking; above were set wooden parapets and gun platforms.
translations.idiomatic: The hull ran sharp below and broad above, with a high stem and stern; three deckhouses rose over the rudder, twin masts bore the sails, and plank shields ran along the sides, topped by wooden battlements and gun mounts.

sentences.zh: 中為四層：最下實土石；

translations.literal: The interior had four levels: the lowest was packed with earth and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Within were four decks: the lowest filled with earth and stone ballast.

sentences.zh: 次寢息所；

translations.literal: Next was the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Above that, the crew's quarters.

sentences.zh: 次左右六門，中置水櫃，揚帆炊爨皆在是，最上如露臺，穴梯而登，傍設翼板，可憑以戰。

translations.literal: Next, six gates left and right; water casks set amidships; hoisting sails and cooking were all there; the topmost was like a terrace, reached by hollowed ladder steps; wing boards set at the sides, on which one could lean to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Then came six doorways to port and starboard with water barrels amidships—sail-handling and the galley both lay here. The topmost deck opened like a terrace, reached by a ladder-well, with fighting platforms on either side.

sentences.zh: 矢石火器皆俯發，可順風行。

translations.literal: Arrows, stones, and firearms were all fired downward; it could run before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows, stones, and gunfire could all be rained downward, and the ship could run before the wind.

sentences.zh: 海蒼視福船稍小。

translations.literal: Haicang compared with Fujian ships was somewhat smaller.
translations.idiomatic: The haicang was slightly smaller than the Fukienese junk.

sentences.zh: 開浪船能容三五十人，頭銳，四槳一櫓，其行如飛，不拘風潮順逆。

translations.literal: Kailang ships could hold thirty to fifty men, sharp at the bow, four oars and one sweep; their travel was like flight, not constrained by wind and tide whether favorable or adverse.
translations.idiomatic: The wave-cutting kailang carried thirty to fifty men, with a sharp prow, four oars and one stern sweep; it skimmed like flight, indifferent to wind and tide.

sentences.zh: 艟暃喬船視海蒼又小。

translations.literal: Chongfei qiao ships compared with haicang were again smaller.
translations.idiomatic: The chongfei qiao was smaller still than the haicang.

sentences.zh: 蒼山船首尾皆闊，帆櫓並用。

translations.literal: Cangshan ships were broad at bow and stern alike; sails and sweeps were both used.
translations.idiomatic: Cangshan craft were wide at both bow and stern, employing sail and oar together.

sentences.zh: 櫓設船傍近後，每傍五枝，每枝五跳，跳二人，以板閘跳上，露首於外，其制上下三層，下實土石，上為戰場，中寢處。

translations.literal: Sweeps were set at the sides near the rear; each side five poles, each pole five treads, two men per tread; boards blocked the treads from above, heads exposed outside; its form had upper, middle, and lower three levels—lower packed with earth and stone, upper for battle, middle for sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Sweeps mounted aft along each rail—five poles per side, five treads per pole, two oarsmen per tread, stepping on boards with heads showing above the gunwale. The hull had three decks: ballast below, sleeping quarters amidships, and the fighting deck aloft.

sentences.zh: 其張帆下椗，皆在上層。

translations.literal: Its raising sails and dropping anchor were all on the upper level.
translations.idiomatic: All sail-handling and anchoring took place on the upper deck.

sentences.zh: 戚繼光云：「倭舟甚小，一入裏海，大福、海蒼不能入，必用蒼船逐之，沖敵便捷，溫人謂之蒼山鐵也。」

translations.literal: Qi Jiguang said: "Wokou boats are very small; once they enter inner seas, large Fujian and haicang ships cannot enter; one must use cang ships to pursue them—charging the enemy with speed—Wen people call them 'Cangshan iron.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jiguang wrote: "The dwarf pirate craft slip into inshore waters where great Fukienese junks and haicang cannot follow—you need cang ships to run them down. They strike fast and handily; men of Wenzhou call them 'Cangshan iron.'

sentences.zh: 沙、鷹二船，相胥成用。

translations.literal: Sha and ying, the two types of ships, mutually assisted in use.
translations.idiomatic: The sha and hawk craft worked as a matched pair.

sentences.zh: 沙船可接戰，然無翼蔽。

translations.literal: Sha ships could engage at close quarters, but lacked wing cover.
translations.idiomatic: The sand-skiff could close for boarding, though it had no flank shielding.

sentences.zh: 鷹船兩端銳，進退如飛。

translations.literal: Ying ships were sharp at both ends; advance and retreat like flight.
translations.idiomatic: The hawk-boat was sharp at bow and stern alike, darting forward or back like a bird in flight.

sentences.zh: 傍釘大茅竹，竹間窗可發銃箭，窗內舷外隱人以蕩槳。

translations.literal: Large bamboo was nailed at the sides; between the bamboo, windows allowed firing muskets and arrows; inside the windows, outside the rail, men hidden to row.
translations.idiomatic: Thick bamboo poles lined the rails, with gunports between them for muskets and arrows, while hidden oarsmen pulled from within, screened from view.

sentences.zh: 先駕此入賊隊，沙船隨進，短兵接戰，無不勝。

translations.literal: First drive these into the enemy ranks; sha ships followed in; close combat—none failed to win.
translations.idiomatic: The hawk-boats led into the pirate line, sand-skiffs followed, and at close quarters they seldom lost.

sentences.zh: 漁船至小，每舟三人，一執布帆，一執槳，一執鳥嘴銃。

translations.literal: Fishing boats were extremely small; each boat three men—one holding cloth sail, one holding oar, one holding bird-beak musket.
translations.idiomatic: Fishing skiffs were tiny—three men per boat: one on the cloth sail, one on the oars, one with a bird-beak musket.

sentences.zh: 隨波上下，可掩賊不備。

translations.literal: Rising and falling with the waves, they could surprise the enemy unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the swells, they could take the enemy unawares.

sentences.zh: 網梭船，定海、臨海、象山俱有之，形如梭。

translations.literal: Net-shuttle boats—Dinghai, Linhai, and Xiangshan all had them; shaped like a shuttle.
translations.idiomatic: Net-shuttle craft were found at Dinghai, Linhai, and Xiangshan, shaped like weaving shuttles.

sentences.zh: 竹桅布帆，僅容二三人，遇風濤輒舁入山麓，可哨探。

translations.literal: Bamboo masts and cloth sails; barely held two or three men; when wind and waves came they were carried into the mountain foothills; could scout.
translations.idiomatic: With bamboo masts and cloth sails, they held only two or three men; in heavy seas they were hauled up into the foothills, and served for reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 蜈蚣船，象形也，能駕佛朗機銃，底尖面闊，兩傍楫數十，行如飛。

translations.literal: Centipede boats—named for their form—could mount Portuguese cannon; bottom sharp, face broad; dozens of oars on both sides; travel like flight.
translations.idiomatic: The centipede boat, named for its shape, mounted falconets; sharp-keeled and broad-beamed, with dozens of oars along either side, it flew over the water.

sentences.zh: 兩頭船，旋轉在舵，因風四馳，諸船無逾其速。

translations.literal: Two-headed boats—turning lay in the rudder; following wind they raced in four directions; no ship exceeded their speed.
translations.idiomatic: The double-prowed craft pivoted on its rudder and ran before the wind in every direction; nothing else matched its speed.

sentences.zh: 蓋自嘉靖以來，東南日備倭，故海舟之制，特詳備云。

translations.literal: Generally, since Jiajing, the southeast daily prepared against wokou; hence the design of sea boats was especially detailed and complete.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiajing onward, the southeast stood on constant guard against pirates, and so the specifications for seagoing vessels were recorded with unusual fullness.

sentences.zh: 明制，馬之屬內廄者曰御馬監，中官掌之，牧於大壩，蓋仿《周禮》十有二閑意。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, horses belonging to the inner stud were called the Imperial Horse Directorate, managed by eunuchs, pastured at Daba—roughly following the Zhou Rites' twelve paddocks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming law, horses of the imperial stud fell to the Imperial Horse Directorate, overseen by eunuchs and grazed at Daba—after the spirit of the Zhou Rites' twelve paddocks.

sentences.zh: 牧於官者，為太僕寺、行太僕寺、苑馬寺及各軍衛，即唐四十八監意。

translations.literal: Those pastured by the state were the Court of the Imperial Stud, traveling Court of the Imperial Stud, Court of Pasturage, and the various military guards—after the Tang's forty-eight directorates.
translations.idiomatic: State herds belonged to the Court of the Imperial Stud, its traveling branches, the Pasturage Courts, and the military guards—descended from the Tang's forty-eight stud offices.

sentences.zh: 牧於民者，南則直隸應天等府，北則直隸及山東、河南等府，即宋保馬意。

translations.literal: Those pastured by the people: in the south, Yingtian and other prefectures of Zhili; in the north, Zhili and Shandong, Henan, and other prefectures—after the Song's horse-rearing households.
translations.idiomatic: Private herds lay in the south in Yingtian and other Zhili prefectures, and in the north across Zhili, Shandong, Henan, and the like—on the Song model of household horse-rearing.

sentences.zh: 其曰備養馬者，始於正統末，選馬給邊，邊馬足，而寄牧於畿甸者也。

translations.literal: Those called reserve-rearing horses began at the end of Zhengtong: horses were selected and sent to the frontier; when frontier horses were sufficient, they were entrusted to pasture in the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve-rearing horses dated from late Zhengtong: selected mounts went to the frontier, and when border herds were full, surplus stock was entrusted to pasture in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 官牧給邊鎮，民牧給京軍，皆有孳生駒。

translations.literal: State herds supplied the border garrisons; private herds supplied the capital armies—both had foals bred.
translations.idiomatic: Official herds fed the frontier garrisons; civilian herds fed the capital troops—both were expected to raise foals.

sentences.zh: 官牧之地曰草場，或為軍民佃種曰熟地，歲徵租佐牧人市馬。

translations.literal: State pasture lands were called pasture grounds, or tilled by soldiers and civilians as cultivated land; rent was levied yearly to help herdsmen buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Official grazing lands were called pasture grounds, though some were farmed by soldiers and civilians as cultivated fields; annual rent helped herders buy replacement horses.

sentences.zh: 牧之人曰恩軍，曰隊軍，曰改編軍，曰充發軍，曰抽發軍。

translations.literal: Those who pastured were called favor soldiers, company soldiers, reorganized soldiers, conscripted soldiers, and drafted soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Herders were drawn from favor troops, company troops, reorganized troops, conscripted troops, and drafted troops.

sentences.zh: 苑馬分三等，上苑萬，中七千，下四千。

translations.literal: Pasturage was divided into three grades: upper pasturage ten thousand, middle seven thousand, lower four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Pasturage was ranked in three grades—upper pastures ten thousand head, middle seven thousand, lower four thousand.

sentences.zh: 一夫牧馬十匹，五十夫設圉長一人。

translations.literal: One man pastured ten horses; for fifty men one stud overseer was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Each herder tended ten horses; every fifty herders had one stud overseer.

sentences.zh: 凡馬肥瘠登耗，籍其毛齒而時省之。

translations.literal: For all horses, fatness, leanness, increase, and decrease were registered by hair and teeth and inspected in season.
translations.idiomatic: Every horse's condition—fat or lean, gain or loss—was logged by coat and teeth and inspected on schedule.

sentences.zh: 三歲，寺卿偕御史印烙，鬻其羸劣以轉市。

translations.literal: At three years, the court director together with the censor branded them and sold the weak and inferior to turn over in the market.
translations.idiomatic: At three years the court director and a censor branded the stock and sold off weak animals to replenish the market.

sentences.zh: 邊衛、營堡、府州縣軍民壯騎操馬，則掌於行寺卿。

translations.literal: Border guards, fortresses, prefectures, counties, and military and civilian mounted drill horses were managed by the traveling court director.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry mounts for border guards, forts, prefectures, counties, and military and civilian drill fell under the traveling court director.

sentences.zh: 邊用不足，又以茶易於番，以貨市於邊。

translations.literal: When the frontier supply was insufficient, tea was again exchanged with the tribes, and goods purchased at the border.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier needs ran short, tea was traded again with frontier peoples, and horses bought locally at the border.

sentences.zh: 其民牧皆視丁田授馬，始曰戶馬，既曰種馬，按歲徵駒。

translations.literal: All private pasturing allotted horses according to household labor and land; at first called household horses, then called breeding horses; foals were levied yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian herds received horses according to household labor and land—first called household horses, then breeding horses—with foals levied each year.

sentences.zh: 種馬死，孳生不及數，輒賠補。

translations.literal: When breeding horses died and foals bred fell short of the quota, compensation was required.
translations.idiomatic: If a breeding mare died or foals fell short of quota, the household had to make good the loss.

sentences.zh: 此其大凡也。

translations.literal: This was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad arrangement.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖都金陵，令應天、太平、鎮江、廬州、鳳陽、揚州六府，滁、和二州民牧馬。

translations.literal: At first, when the Founding Emperor made Nanjing his capital, he ordered the six prefectures of Yingtian, Taiping, Zhenjiang, Luzhou, Fengyang, and Yangzhou and the two prefectures of Chu and He to pasture horses for the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongwu Emperor first established his capital at Nanjing, he ordered the people of Yingtian, Taiping, Zhenjiang, Luzhou, Fengyang, Yangzhou, and the prefectures of Chu and He to raise horses.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，設太僕寺於滁州，統於兵部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, the Court of the Imperial Stud was established at Chuzhou, subordinate to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 6 the Court of the Imperial Stud was set up at Chuzhou under the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 後增滁陽五牧監，領四十八羣。

translations.literal: Later five pasture directorates were added at Chuyang, overseeing forty-eight herds.
translations.idiomatic: Five pasture directorates were later added at Chuyang, overseeing forty-eight herds.

sentences.zh: 已，為四十監，旋罷，惟存天長、大興、舒城三監。

translations.literal: Soon there were forty directorates; then they were abolished, and only the three directorates of Tianchang, Daxing, and Shucheng remained.
translations.idiomatic: The number rose to forty directorates, then most were abolished, leaving only Tianchang, Daxing, and Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 置草場於湯泉、滁州等地。

translations.literal: Pasture grounds were established at Tangquan, Chuzhou, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture grounds were laid out at Tangquan, Chuzhou, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 復令飛熊、廣武、英武三衛，五軍養一馬，馬歲生駒，一歲解京。

translations.literal: Again he ordered the three guards of Feixiong, Guangwu, and Yingwu: five armies reared one horse; horses yearly bore foals; at one year they were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered the Feixiong, Guangwu, and Yingwu guards to raise one horse per five armies; foals born each year were sent to the capital at one year old.

sentences.zh: 既而以監牧歸有司，專令民牧。

translations.literal: Then pasture directorates were returned to the local officials, and the people alone were ordered to pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture directorates were then returned to local officials, and civilian horse-rearing alone was mandated.

sentences.zh: 江南十一戶，江北五戶養馬一，復其身。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze, eleven households; north of the Yangtze, five households reared one horse; their corvée service was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river eleven households, north of the river five, raised one horse apiece, and their labor service was remitted.

sentences.zh: 太僕官督理，歲正月至六月報定駒，七月至十月報顯駒，十一、二月報重駒。

translations.literal: Court of the Imperial Stud officials supervised; from the first to the sixth month they reported fixed foals, from the seventh to the tenth reported visible foals, from the eleventh to the twelfth reported heavy foals.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Stud officials supervised the work: January through June brought reports of registered foals, July through October of weaned foals, November and December of yearling foals.

sentences.zh: 歲終考馬政，以法治府州縣官吏。

translations.literal: At year's end horse policy was examined, and prefectural, county, and district officials were punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end horse policy was audited, and prefectural and county officials were held to account by law.

sentences.zh: 凡牡曰兒，牝曰騍。

translations.literal: Generally, male was called er; female was called ke.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions were called er; mares, ke.

sentences.zh: 兒一、騍四為羣，羣頭一人。

translations.literal: One er and four ke made a herd; one herd head.
translations.idiomatic: One stallion and four mares formed a herd, with one herd head.

sentences.zh: 五羣，羣長一人。

translations.literal: Five herds, one herd chief.
translations.idiomatic: Every five herds had one herd chief.

sentences.zh: 三十年，設北平、遼東、山西、陝西、甘肅行太僕寺，定牧馬草場。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, traveling Courts of the Imperial Stud were established at Beiping, Liaodong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Gansu, fixing horse pasture grounds.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year traveling Imperial Stud courts were set up in Beiping, Liaodong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Gansu, with pasture grounds fixed for each.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，設太僕寺於北京，掌順天、山東、河南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, the Court of the Imperial Stud was established at Beijing, managing Shuntian, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle the Court of the Imperial Stud was established at Beijing, overseeing Shuntian, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 舊設者為南太僕寺，掌應天等六府二州。

translations.literal: The previously established one became the Southern Court of the Imperial Stud, managing Yingtian and the other six prefectures and two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The older office became the Southern Court of the Imperial Stud, in charge of Yingtian and the other six prefectures and two sub-prefectures.

sentences.zh: 四年，設苑馬寺於陝西、甘肅，統六監，監統四苑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Court of Pasturage was established in Shaanxi and Gansu, overseeing six directorates; each directorate oversaw four pastures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Pasturage Courts were established in Shaanxi and Gansu, each overseeing six directorates and each directorate four pastures.

sentences.zh: 又設北京、遼東二苑馬寺，所統視陝西、甘肅。

translations.literal: Beijing and Liaodong Pasturage Courts were also established; what they oversaw matched Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Pasturage Courts were also set up in Beijing and Liaodong on the same model as Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，令北畿民計丁養馬，選居閑官教之畜牧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the people of the northern capital districts were ordered to pasture horses by counted labor; idle officials were selected to teach them animal husbandry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the northern capital districts were ordered to raise horses by household count, with selected idle officials to teach them husbandry.

sentences.zh: 民十五丁以下一匹，十六丁以上二匹，為事編發者七戶一匹，得除罪。

translations.literal: Households of fifteen labor or below, one horse; sixteen labor or above, two horses; those conscripted for service, seven households one horse, gaining remission of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Households of fifteen laborers or fewer kept one horse; those of sixteen or more, two; men conscripted for penal service kept one horse per seven households and earned remission of sentence.

sentences.zh: 尋以寺卿楊砥言，北方人戶五丁養一，免其田租之半，薊州以東至南海等衛，戍守軍外，每軍飼種馬一。

translations.literal: Soon, at Court Director Yang Di's word, northerners five labor per household reared one, half their land tax remitted; from east of Jizhou to the Nanhai and other guards, aside from garrison troops, each soldier fed one breeding horse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Court Director Yang Di's advice, northerners raised one horse per five laborers with half their land tax remitted; from east of Jizhou to Nanhai and other guards, every garrison soldier outside frontier duty fed one breeding mare.

sentences.zh: 又定南方養馬例：鳳、廬、揚、滁、和五丁一，應天、太、鎮十丁一。

translations.literal: Southern horse-rearing regulations were also fixed: Feng, Lu, Yang, Chu, and He five labor one; Yingtian, Tai, and Zhen ten labor one.
translations.idiomatic: Southern quotas were also set: Fengyang, Luzhou, Yangzhou, Chuzhou, and He five laborers per horse; Yingtian, Taiping, and Zhenjiang ten per horse.

sentences.zh: 淮、徐初養馬，亦以丁為率。

translations.literal: Huai and Xu at first also pastured horses, likewise by labor as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and Xu at first raised horses too, on the same labor quota.

sentences.zh: 十八年，罷北京苑馬寺，悉牧之民。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Beijing Pasturage Court was abolished; all were pastured by the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Beijing Pasturage Court was abolished and all herds passed to civilian keepers.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，以南土不產馬，改徵銀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua, because southern soil did not produce horses, collection was changed to silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 2, since the south could not breed horses, the levy was changed to silver.

sentences.zh: 四年，始建太僕寺常盈庫，貯備用馬價。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Court of the Imperial Stud's Ever-Full Treasury was first built, storing reserve horse prices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Imperial Stud's Ever-Full Treasury was established to hold funds for reserve horse purchases.

sentences.zh: 是時，民漸苦養馬。

translations.literal: At that time, the people gradually suffered from horse-rearing.
translations.idiomatic: By then the burden of horse-rearing was growing on the people.

sentences.zh: 六年，吏部侍郎葉盛言：「向時歲課一駒，而民不擾者，以芻牧地廣，民得為生也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Vice Minister of Personnel Ye Sheng said: "Formerly the yearly levy was one foal, yet the people were not disturbed, because pasture lands were broad and the people could make a living.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Vice Minister of Personnel Ye Sheng memorialized: "When the yearly levy was one foal per household, the people bore it because pasture was ample and they could still live.

sentences.zh: 自豪右莊田漸多，養馬漸不足。

translations.literal: Since grandee and minister estates gradually grew, horse-rearing gradually fell short.
translations.idiomatic: But as estates of the great and powerful spread, grazing land shrank and herds fell short.

sentences.zh: 洪熙初，改兩年一駒，成化初，改三年一駒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongxi, it was changed to one foal every two years; at the beginning of Chenghua, to one foal every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi reduced the levy to one foal every two years; Chenghua again to one every three.

sentences.zh: 馬愈削，民愈貧。

translations.literal: Horses grew ever fewer; the people grew ever poorer.
translations.idiomatic: Horses dwindled while the people grew poorer.

sentences.zh: 然馬卒不可少，乃復兩年一駒之制，民愈不堪。

translations.literal: Yet horses ultimately could not be few; the two-year-one-foal system was restored, and the people were yet more unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet horses could not be done without, so the two-year levy was restored—and the people were squeezed harder still.

sentences.zh: 請敕邊鎮隨俗所宜，凡可以買馬足邊、軍民交益者，便宜處置。」

translations.literal: He requested an edict to the border garrisons to follow local custom as suited; whatever could buy horses to fill the border and benefit soldiers and civilians alike, let it be done as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that border garrisons be authorized to do whatever local conditions allowed—buying horses to fill frontier needs and easing the burden on soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 時馬文升撫陝西，又極論邊軍償馬之累，請令屯田卒田多丁少而不領馬者，歲輸銀一錢，以助賠償。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Wensheng was grand coordinator of Shaanxi; he also argued at length on the burden of border troops compensating for horses, requesting that garrison farmers with much land and few laborers who did not receive horses pay one mace of silver yearly to aid compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wensheng, then grand coordinator of Shaanxi, likewise detailed the toll of frontier compensation and proposed that garrison farmers with ample land but few laborers who took no horses pay one mace of silver yearly toward indemnities.

sentences.zh: 雖皆允行，而民困不能舒也。

translations.literal: Although all were approved and carried out, the people's hardship could not be eased.
translations.idiomatic: Though all this was approved, the people's distress did not lift.

sentences.zh: 繼文升撫陝者蕭禎，請省行太僕寺。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhen, who succeeded Wensheng as grand coordinator of Shaanxi, requested abolishing the traveling Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhen, who succeeded Ma Wensheng in Shaanxi, asked to abolish the traveling Imperial Stud court.

sentences.zh: 兵部覆云：「洪、永時，設行太僕及苑馬寺，凡茶馬、番人貢馬，悉收寺、苑放牧，常數萬匹，足充邊用。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War replied: "In the Hongwu and Yongle periods, traveling Imperial Stud courts and Pasturage Courts were established; all tea-horse and tribal tribute horses were received by the courts and pastures for grazing—regularly tens of thousands of horses, sufficient to fill frontier use.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War answered: "Under Hongwu and Yongle, traveling stud courts and pasturage offices took in all tea-horse and tribute stock—tens of thousands at a time, enough for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 正統以後，北敵屢入抄掠，馬遂日耗。

translations.literal: After Zhengtong, northern enemies repeatedly entered to raid and plunder; horses daily dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengtong, northern raids wore the herds down day by day.

sentences.zh: 言者每請裁革，是惜小費而忘大計。」

translations.literal: Critics each requested cutting and abolishing; this was cherishing small expense and forgetting the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Critics repeatedly urged cuts—but that was penny-wise and pound-foolish.

sentences.zh: 於是敕諭禎，但令加意督察。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict instructed Zhen, but only ordered him to supervise with care.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to Zhen bidding him supervise more closely, but not to abolish the office.

sentences.zh: 而北畿自永樂以來，馬日滋，輒責民牧，民年十五者即養馬。

translations.literal: Yet in the northern capital districts since Yongle, horses daily multiplied; the people were repeatedly charged to pasture; people aged fifteen and above at once pastured horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Yongle onward in the northern capital districts herds grew and the people were repeatedly pressed to keep them—every youth of fifteen was put to horse-rearing at once.

sentences.zh: 太僕少卿彭禮以戶丁有限，而課駒無窮，請定種馬額。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Peng Li, because household labor was limited yet foal levies were endless, requested fixing the breeding-horse quota.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Peng Li, noting that household labor was finite while foal levies were not, asked that breeding quotas be fixed.

sentences.zh: 會文升為兵部尚書，奏行其請，乃定兩京太僕種馬，兒馬二萬五千，騍馬四之，二年納駒，著為令。

translations.literal: When Wensheng became Minister of War, he memorialized to carry out the request; then breeding horses of the two-court Imperial Stud were fixed: er horses twenty-five thousand, ke horses four times that; foals submitted every two years—established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Wensheng became Minister of War he carried the proposal through: the two Imperial Stud courts were capped at twenty-five thousand stallions and four times as many mares, with foals due every two years—written into law.

sentences.zh: 時弘治六年也。

translations.literal: At that time it was the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was Hongzhi 6.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，尚書劉大夏薦南京太常卿楊一清為副都御史，督理陝西馬政。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year, Minister Liu Daxia recommended Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Yang Yiqing as vice censor-in-chief to supervise Shaanxi horse policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year Minister Liu Daxia recommended Yang Yiqing, director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices, as vice censor-in-chief to oversee Shaanxi horse policy.

sentences.zh: 一清奏言：「我朝以陝右宜牧，設監苑，跨二千餘里。

translations.literal: Yiqing memorialized: "Our dynasty, because the right of Shaanxi suited pasturing, established directorate pastures spanning more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing memorialized: "Our dynasty, finding western Shaanxi ideal for grazing, established directorate pastures spanning more than two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 後皆廢，惟存長樂、靈武二監。

translations.literal: Later all were abolished; only the two directorates of Changle and Lingwu remained.
translations.idiomatic: Most were later abolished; only the Changle and Lingwu directorates survived.

sentences.zh: 今牧地止數百里，然以供西邊尚無不足，但苦監牧非人，牧養無法耳。

translations.literal: Now pasture lands amounted to only several hundred li, yet to supply the western border there was still no insufficiency; but the hardship lay in unworthy pasture officials and lawless husbandry.
translations.idiomatic: Today grazing land covers only a few hundred li, yet still suffices for the western frontier—the trouble is unworthy officials and slipshod husbandry.

sentences.zh: 兩監六苑，開城、安定水泉便利，宜為上苑，牧萬馬；

translations.literal: The two directorates and six pastures: Kaicheng and Anding had convenient springs; they should be upper pastures, pasturing ten thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Of the two directorates' six pastures, Kaicheng and Anding enjoy good water and should rank as upper pastures, grazing ten thousand head.

sentences.zh: 廣甯、萬安為中苑；

translations.literal: Guangning and Wan'an as middle pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Guangning and Wan'an should serve as middle pastures.

sentences.zh: 黑水草場逼窄，清平地狹土瘠，為下苑。

translations.literal: Heishui pasture ground was cramped and narrow; Qingping land was narrow and soil poor—as lower pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Heishui pasture is cramped, and Qingping's soil is thin and poor—they should rank as lower pastures.

sentences.zh: 萬安可五千，廣寧四千，清平二千，黑水千五百。

translations.literal: Wan'an could hold five thousand, Guangning four thousand, Qingping two thousand, Heishui one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'an could carry five thousand head, Guangning four thousand, Qingping two thousand, and Heishui fifteen hundred.

sentences.zh: 六苑歲給軍外，可常牧馬三萬二千五百，足供三邊用。

translations.literal: Beyond the six pastures' yearly supply to the army, they could regularly pasture thirty-two thousand five hundred horses, sufficient to supply the three frontiers' use.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from what the six pastures owed the army each year, they could maintain thirty-two thousand five hundred horses—enough for all three frontiers.

sentences.zh: 然欲廣孳息，必多蓄種馬，宜增滿萬匹，兩年一駒，五年可足前數。

translations.literal: Yet to broaden breeding increase, one must store many breeding mares; it is fitting to increase to the full ten thousand head—a foal every two years—and in five years one could fill the prior number.
translations.idiomatic: To expand the herd, however, they would need more brood stock: raise breeding mares to ten thousand, expect a foal every two years, and in five years the target herd could be reached.

sentences.zh: 請支太僕馬價銀四萬二千兩，於平、慶、臨、鞏買種馬七千。

translations.literal: Request disbursement of forty-two thousand taels of silver from the Imperial Stud horse-price funds, to buy seven thousand breeding mares in Ping, Qing, Lin, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that forty-two thousand taels of stud-horse silver be released to buy seven thousand brood mares in Ping, Qing, Lin, and Gong.

sentences.zh: 又養馬恩隊軍不足，請編流亡民及問遣回籍者，且視恩軍例，凡發邊衛充軍者，改令各苑牧馬，增為三千人。

translations.literal: Also horse-rearing Favor Corps troops were insufficient; request enrolling displaced persons and those interrogated and sent back to native districts, and following the favor-troops precedent—wherever men sent to frontier guards as conscript soldiers, order them instead to pasture horses at each pasture, increase to three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Favor Corps assigned to horse-rearing was also understrength. He asked that displaced persons and those interrogated and sent home be enrolled under the Favor Corps precedent, and that convicts dispatched to frontier guards be reassigned instead to pasture duty at the various ranches—bringing the force up to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 又請相地勢，築城通商，種植榆柳，春夏放牧，秋冬還廄，馬既得安，敵來亦可收保。」

translations.literal: Also request selecting sites by terrain, building walls to open trade, planting elms and willows—grazing in spring and summer, returning to stables in autumn and winter—so horses would be secure and could be brought to safety when enemies came.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed choosing ground by terrain, building walls to open trade, and planting elms and willows: graze in spring and summer, return to the stables in autumn and winter. Horses would be kept safe—and when enemies came, they could be gathered in and defended.

sentences.zh: 孝宗方重邊防，大夏掌兵部，一清所奏輒行。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong was then emphasizing frontier defense; Daxia held the Ministry of War; every proposal Yiqing submitted was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong was then putting weight on frontier defense. Liu Daxia headed the Ministry of War, and every memorial Yiqing submitted was promptly enacted.

sentences.zh: 遷總制仍督馬政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand coordinator while still supervising horse policy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand coordinator while continuing to oversee horse policy.

sentences.zh: 諸監草場，原額十三萬三千七百餘頃，存者已不及半。

translations.literal: Directorate pasture lands originally totaled one hundred thirty-three thousand seven hundred-odd qing; what remained was not even half.
translations.idiomatic: The directorates' pasture lands had originally totaled more than 133,700 qing; less than half now survived.

sentences.zh: 一清核之，得荒地十二萬八千餘頃，又開武安苑地二千九百餘頃。

translations.literal: Yiqing audited them and recovered one hundred twenty-eight thousand-odd qing of wasteland, and opened two thousand nine hundred-odd qing for the Wu'an pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing audited the registers and recovered more than 128,000 qing of wasteland, and opened nearly 2,900 qing for the Wu'an pasture.

sentences.zh: 正德二年聞於朝。

translations.literal: In Zhengde 2 it was reported at court.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 2 the results were reported at court.

sentences.zh: 及一清去官，未幾復廢。

translations.literal: After Yiqing left office, before long it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After Yiqing left office, the reforms were soon abandoned again.

sentences.zh: 時御史王濟言：「民苦養馬。

translations.literal: At that time Censor Wang Ji said: "The people suffer from horse-rearing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Censor Wang Ji said: "The people are crushed by the burden of raising horses.

sentences.zh: 有一孳生馬，輒害之。

translations.literal: Whenever they had a breeding horse, they would kill it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a mare foaled, they would kill the foal.

sentences.zh: 間有定駒，賂醫諱之，有顯駒墜落之。

translations.literal: Occasionally when a foal was fixed, they bribed the vet to conceal it; when a foal was obvious, they made it fall and die.
translations.idiomatic: If a foal was already registered, they bribed the veterinarian to hide it; if a foal was plainly visible, they contrived a fall to kill it.

sentences.zh: 馬虧欠不過納銀二兩，既孳生者已聞官，而復倒斃，不過納銀三兩，孳生不死則饑餓。

translations.literal: A horse shortage required payment of only two taels of silver; if a breeding horse had already been reported to officials and then died suddenly, payment was only three taels; if breeding stock did not die, they starved it.
translations.idiomatic: A shortfall in horses cost only two taels of silver to settle. Once a foal had been reported to the authorities, a sudden death required only three taels—but if the breeding stock lived, they starved it instead.

sentences.zh: 馬日瘦削，無濟實用。

translations.literal: Horses daily grew thinner—of no practical use.
translations.idiomatic: The horses wasted away day by day, useless for any real purpose.

sentences.zh: 今種馬、地畝、人丁，歲取有定額，請以其額數令民買馬，而種馬孳生，縣官無與。」

translations.literal: Now breeding horses, acreage, and population each have fixed yearly quotas—request using those quota numbers to have the people buy horses, while breeding and reproduction be none of the county magistrate's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Breeding stock, acreage, and household quotas are already fixed each year. Let the people buy horses to those quotas instead, and leave breeding entirely out of the county magistrate's hands.

sentences.zh: 兵部是其言。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War agreed.

sentences.zh: 自後，每有奏報，輒引濟言縣官無與種馬事，但責駒於民，遺母求子矣。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever memorials were submitted, Ji's words were cited that county officials had nothing to do with breeding horses but only demand foals from the people—leaving the mare and demanding the foal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever horse policy was debated, officials cited Ji's argument that magistrates should have nothing to do with breeding stock and need only demand foals from the people—demanding the child while abandoning the mother.

sentences.zh: 初，邊臣請馬，太僕寺以見馬給之。

translations.literal: At first, when frontier officials requested horses, the Court of Imperial Stud supplied available horses.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when frontier officials requested horses, the Court of Imperial Stud issued horses from its herds.

sentences.zh: 自改徵銀，馬日少，而請者相繼，給價十萬，買馬萬匹。

translations.literal: Since the change to collecting silver, horses daily grew fewer while requesters followed one after another—given one hundred thousand in price to buy ten thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Once the system shifted to silver payments, the stud's herds shrank while requests kept coming—100,000 taels disbursed to buy ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 邊臣不能市良馬，馬多死，太僕卿儲巏以為言，請仍給馬。

translations.literal: Frontier officials could not purchase good horses; many died. Director of the Imperial Stud Chu Juan spoke on this and requested that horses again be supplied directly.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials could not buy sound horses on the market, and many died in transit. Director Chu Juan of the Imperial Stud protested and asked that horses be issued again in kind.

sentences.zh: 又指陳各邊種馬盜賣私借之弊。

translations.literal: He also pointed out abuses of breeding horses being stolen, sold, and privately lent along the various frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He also detailed how breeding stock along the frontiers was stolen, sold off, and lent out in private arrangements.

sentences.zh: 語雖切，不能從。

translations.literal: Though his words were pointed, they could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: His warnings were sharp, but they went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 而邊鎮給發日益繁。

translations.literal: Yet frontier garrisons' disbursements grew daily more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile frontier garrisons' demands for horses and funds grew ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 延綏三十六營堡，自弘治十一年始，十年間，發太僕銀二十八萬有奇，買補四萬九千餘匹，寧夏、大同、居庸關等處不與焉。

translations.literal: The thirty-six camps and forts of Yansui, from Hongzhi 11 onward—in ten years Imperial Stud silver of two hundred eighty thousand-odd was disbursed to buy and replace forty-nine thousand-odd horses, not counting Ningxia, Datong, Juyong Pass, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: For Yansui's thirty-six camps and forts alone, from Hongzhi 11 through the next decade, the Imperial Stud spent more than 280,000 taels to buy and replace nearly 49,000 horses—and that does not include Ningxia, Datong, Juyong Pass, or the other sectors.

sentences.zh: 至正德七年，遂開納馬例，凡十二條。

translations.literal: By Zhengde 7, the horse-contribution statute was opened—twelve articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhengde 7 the court opened a horse-contribution statute of twelve articles.

sentences.zh: 九年，復發太僕銀市馬萬五千于山東、遼東、河南及鳳陽、保定諸府。

translations.literal: Year 9: Imperial Stud silver was again disbursed to purchase fifteen thousand horses in Shandong, Liaodong, Henan, and Fenyang, Baoding, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the Imperial Stud again released funds to buy fifteen thousand horses in Shandong, Liaodong, Henan, and the prefectures of Fengyang, Baoding, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，陝西苑馬少卿盧璧條上馬政，請督逋負、明印烙、訓醫藥、均地差，以救目前，而闢場廣蓄為經久計。

translations.literal: Jiajing 1: Vice Director of Shaanxi Pasture Horses Lu Bi submitted a detailed plan on horse policy, requesting supervision of arrears, clear branding, medical training, and equalized land assignments—to save the present—while opening pastures and broadening reserves as a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 Lu Bi, vice director of Shaanxi pasture horses, submitted a detailed horse-policy plan: collect arrears, enforce branding, train veterinarians, and equalize land assignments to stave off immediate collapse, while opening new pastures and building reserves for the long term.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the plan and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 自後言馬事者頗眾，大都因事立說，補救一時而已。

translations.literal: Afterward those speaking on horse affairs were quite numerous; mostly they framed arguments according to circumstances, patching only for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: After that, memorials on horse policy multiplied, but most were ad hoc fixes—remedies for the crisis of the moment, not lasting reform.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，俺答入寇，太僕馬缺，復行正德納馬例。

translations.literal: Year 29: Altan invaded; Imperial Stud horses were short; the Zhengde horse-contribution statute was again implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 Altan raided the frontier; the Imperial Stud's herds were depleted, and the Zhengde horse-contribution statute was revived.

sentences.zh: 已，稍增損之。

translations.literal: Later it was slightly increased and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Its terms were later adjusted, expanded here and trimmed there.

sentences.zh: 至四十一年，遂開例至捐馬授職。

translations.literal: By year 41, the statute was opened to the point of donating horses for offices.
translations.idiomatic: By year 41 the statute had widened until men could donate horses in exchange for official appointments.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，提督四夷館太常少卿武金言：「種馬之設，專為孳生備用。

translations.literal: Longqing 2: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Supervisor of the Four Barbarian Hostels Wu Jin said: "Breeding horses were established solely for breeding and reserve use.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 2 Wu Jin, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of the Four Barbarian Hostels, said: "Breeding stock exists only to propagate the herd and fill the reserves.

sentences.zh: 備用馬既別買，則種馬可遂省。

translations.literal: Since reserve horses are now purchased separately, breeding stock can be done away with.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve horses are now bought separately, so breeding stock can be abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 今備用馬已足三萬，宜令每馬折銀三十兩，解太僕。

translations.literal: Now reserve horses already reach thirty thousand—it is fitting to have each horse converted to thirty taels of silver and delivered to the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve horses already number thirty thousand. Let each be commuted at thirty taels of silver and paid into the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 種馬盡賣，輸兵部，一馬十兩，則直隸、山東、河南十二萬匹，可得銀百二十萬，且收草豆銀二十四萬。」

translations.literal: Sell all breeding horses and turn proceeds over to the Ministry of War—ten taels per horse—then from Zhili, Shandong, and Henan's one hundred twenty thousand horses, one million two hundred thousand taels could be obtained, and additionally collect two hundred forty thousand taels in fodder-bean silver.
translations.idiomatic: Sell all breeding stock and remit the proceeds to the Ministry of War at ten taels per horse. From the 120,000 horses in Zhili, Shandong, and Henan alone the state would gain 1.2 million taels, plus another 240,000 taels in fodder and bean-money assessments.

sentences.zh: 御史謝廷傑謂：「祖制所定，關軍機，不可廢。」

translations.literal: Censor Xie Tingjie said: "What ancestral institutions established concerns military affairs and cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xie Tingjie objected: "What the founding institutions fixed touches military readiness and must not be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 兵部是廷傑言。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War approved Tingjie's words.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War sided with Tingjie.

sentences.zh: 而是時，內帑乏，方分使括天下逋賦。

translations.literal: But at that time the inner treasury was depleted; commissioners were being dispatched to collect nationwide tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: But the inner treasury was empty, and commissioners were already fanning out to squeeze tax arrears from every province.

sentences.zh: 穆宗可金奏，下部議。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong approved Jin's memorial and sent it to the ministries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong approved Jin's memorial and referred it to the ministries for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 部請養、賣各半，從之。

translations.literal: The ministries requested half kept and half sold—the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries proposed keeping half the herds and selling half; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 太僕之有銀也，自成化時始，然止三萬餘兩。

translations.literal: The Imperial Stud's possession of silver began from the Chenghua period, yet it amounted to only thirty-odd thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Stud first accumulated silver under Chenghua, but the total was only a little over thirty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 及種馬賣，銀日增。

translations.literal: When breeding horses were sold, silver daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Once breeding stock went on the block, the silver poured in.

sentences.zh: 是時，通貢互市所貯亦無幾。

translations.literal: At that time, what was stored from tribute trade and mutual markets was also slight.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, reserves from tribute trade and frontier markets were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 及張居正作輔，力主盡賣之議。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng became chief minister, he strongly advocated selling all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng became chief minister, he pushed hard to sell off the herds entirely.

sentences.zh: 自萬曆九年始，上馬八兩，下至五兩，又折徵草豆地租，銀益多，以供團營買馬及各邊之請。

translations.literal: From Wanli 9 onward, upper-grade horses at eight taels, down to five taels; also converting collection of pasture fodder and land rent—silver grew ever more, to supply the Capital Garrison Corps' horse purchases and requests from all frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: From Wanli 9 onward, upper-grade horses were commuted at eight taels and lower grades at five; fodder and pasture rents were converted to silver as well. The treasury swelled—enough to buy horses for the Capital Garrison Corps and meet every frontier request.

sentences.zh: 然一騸馬輒發三十金，而州縣以駑馬進，其直止數金。

translations.literal: Yet for one gelding thirty gold was disbursed, while prefectures and counties presented scrub horses whose value was only a few gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court paid thirty taels for a single gelding while prefectures and counties delivered nags worth only a few taels apiece.

sentences.zh: 且仍寄養於馬戶，害民不減曩時。

translations.literal: Moreover they were still board-reared with horse households—the harm to the people no less than before.
translations.idiomatic: The horses were still lodged with horse-rearing households, and the burden on the people was no lighter than before.

sentences.zh: 又國家有興作、賞賚，往往借支太僕銀，太僕帑益耗。

translations.literal: Also for state construction and rewards, Imperial Stud silver was often borrowed—the stud treasury grew ever more depleted.
translations.idiomatic: State construction and imperial rewards also drew repeated loans from the stud treasury, draining it further.

sentences.zh: 十五年，寺卿羅應鶴請禁支借。

translations.literal: Year 15: Director Luo Yinghe requested forbidding such borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Director Luo Yinghe asked that such borrowing be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 二十四年詔太僕給陝西賞功銀。

translations.literal: Year 24: an edict ordered the Imperial Stud to supply Shaanxi reward silver.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 an edict ordered the Imperial Stud to supply reward silver for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 寺臣言：「先年庫積四百餘萬，自東西二役興，僅餘四之一。

translations.literal: Court officials said: "In earlier years the treasury accumulated over four million; since the eastern and western campaigns arose, only a quarter remained.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the court protested: "The treasury once held more than four million taels. After the eastern and western campaigns, only a quarter was left.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮用兵，百萬之積俱空。

translations.literal: The Korea campaign emptied the million-strong reserve entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The war in Korea emptied even that million-tael reserve.

sentences.zh: 今所存者，止十餘萬。

translations.literal: What remains now is only a hundred-odd thousand.
translations.idiomatic: What remains today is barely a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 況本寺寄養馬歲額二萬匹，今歲取折色，則馬之派徵甚少，而東徵調兌尤多。

translations.literal: Moreover this office's board-reared horses yearly quota is twenty thousand; now with yearly collection in commutation, horse assessments are very few, while eastern campaign requisitions and exchanges are especially many.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this office still owes twenty thousand board-reared horses each year, yet commutation has reduced actual horse levies to a trickle while eastern campaign requisitions and transfers grow ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 卒然有警，馬與銀俱竭，何以應之。」

translations.literal: If alarm came suddenly, horses and silver would both be exhausted—how to respond?
translations.idiomatic: If alarm struck suddenly, both horses and silver would be gone—how could we answer it?

sentences.zh: 章下部，未能有所釐革也。

translations.literal: The memorial went to the ministries; no reform could be effected.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the ministries, but nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，核戶兵工三部，借支太僕馬價至一千三百餘萬。

translations.literal: Early Chongzhen: auditing the ministries of Revenue, War, and Works—borrowing from Imperial Stud horse funds reached over thirteen million.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen, an audit of the ministries of Revenue, War, and Works found that borrowing from Imperial Stud horse funds had reached more than thirteen million taels.

sentences.zh: 蓋自萬曆以來，冏政大壞，而邊牧廢弛，愈不可問。

translations.literal: From Wanli onward stud administration was greatly corrupted, and frontier pasturing abandoned and lax—ever more beyond inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wanli reign onward stud administration collapsed, and frontier grazing fell into ruin beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 既而遼東督師袁崇煥以缺馬，請於兩京州縣寄養馬內，折三千匹價買之西邊。

translations.literal: Then Liaodong supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan, for lack of horses, requested commutation of three thousand board-reared horses from the two capitals' prefectures and counties to purchase horses on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yuan Chonghuan, supreme commander in Liaodong, citing a horse shortage, asked to commute three thousand board-reared horses from the prefectures and counties of the two capitals and use the proceeds to buy horses for the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 太僕卿塗國鼎言：「祖宗令民養馬，專供京營騎操，防護都城，非為邊也。

translations.literal: Director Tu Guoding said: "Our ancestors had the people raise horses solely to supply the capital garrison's cavalry drill and protect the capital—not for the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Director Tu Guoding argued: "Our ancestors made the people raise horses solely to mount and drill the capital garrisons and defend the throne—not to supply the frontiers.
