sentences.zh: 後來改折，無事則易馬輸銀，有警則出銀市馬，仍是為京師備禦之意。

translations.literal: The later change to commutation: in peace, exchange horses for silver tribute; in alarm, disburse silver to buy horses—still the intent of provisioning the capital's defense.
translations.idiomatic: The later shift to commutation kept the same logic: in peace, horses were exchanged for silver; in crisis, silver bought horses—always to keep the capital armed.

sentences.zh: 今折銀已多給各鎮，如並此馬盡折，萬一變生，奈何？」

translations.literal: Now commuted silver has largely gone to the various garrisons—if even these horses are all commuted, should crisis arise, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Commuted silver has already flowed largely to the frontier garrisons. If these last horses are commuted too, what happens when crisis comes?

sentences.zh: 帝是其言，卻崇煥請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and rejected Chonghuan's request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and rejected Chonghuan's request.

sentences.zh: 按明世馬政，法久弊叢。

translations.literal: Examining Ming horse policy: the law long degenerated into a tangle of abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying Ming horse policy as a whole, the statutes had long since rotted into a thicket of abuses.

sentences.zh: 其始盛終衰之故，大率由草場興廢。

translations.literal: The reasons for flourishing at the start and decline at the end were largely tied to the rise and fall of pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: Its rise and fall, broadly speaking, tracked the gain and loss of pasture land.

sentences.zh: 太祖既設草場於大江南北，復定北邊牧地：自東勝以西至寧夏、河西、察罕腦兒，以東至大同、宣府、開平，又東南至大寧、遼東，抵鴨綠江又北千里，而南至各衛分守地，又自雁門關西抵黃河外，東曆紫荊、居庸、古北抵山海衛。

translations.literal: Taizu, having established pastures south and north of the Yangtze, also fixed northern frontier grazing lands: from Dongsheng westward to Ningxia, Hexi, and Chaghan Nur; eastward to Datong, Xuanfu, and Kaiping; southeast again to Daning and Liaodong, reaching the Yalu River and northward a thousand li; southward to each guard's allotted defense lands; and from Yanmen Pass west to beyond the Yellow River, east through Zijing, Juyong, and Gubei to Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu established pastures across the lands south and north of the Yangtze, then set aside northern grazing grounds: from Dongsheng west to Ningxia, Hexi, and Chaghan Nur; east to Datong, Xuanfu, and Kaiping; southeast to Daning and Liaodong as far as the Yalu and a thousand li beyond; south to each guard's allotted defense zone; and from Yanmen Pass west beyond the Yellow River, east through Zijing, Juyong, and Gubei to Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 荒閑平埜，非軍民屯種者，聽諸王駙馬以至近邊軍民樵採牧放，在邊籓府不得自佔。

translations.literal: Waste and idle flat lands where military and civilians did not farm—princes, imperial sons-in-law, down to frontier military and civilians were permitted to gather firewood, graze, and pasture; frontier princely establishments could not occupy them for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Idle plains that neither soldiers nor civilians farmed were open—from princes and imperial sons-in-law down to frontier soldiers and commoners—for firewood, grazing, and pasturing. Frontier princely estates could not seize them for private use.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，又置草場於畿甸。

translations.literal: In Yongle's reign, pastures were also established in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle, pastures were also set aside in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 尋以順聖川至桑乾河百三十餘里，水草美，令乙太僕千騎，令懷來衛卒百人分牧，後增至萬二千匹。

translations.literal: Soon, as from Shunshheng River to Sanggan River over one hundred thirty li the water and grass were fine, ordered one thousand Imperial Stud riders, ordered one hundred Huailai Guard soldiers to pasture separately—later increased to twelve thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, finding the stretch from Shunshheng River to Sanggan River—more than 130 li of fine grass and water—the court assigned a thousand Imperial Stud riders and a hundred soldiers of Huailai Guard to graze the land in shifts. The herd later grew to twelve thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，復置九馬坊於保安州。

translations.literal: Early Xuande: the Nine Horse Paddocks were restored in Bao'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xuande the Nine Horse Paddocks were restored in Bao'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是兵部奏，馬大蕃息，以色別而名之，其毛色二十五等，其種三百六十。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of War memorialized: horses greatly multiplied; they were named by color distinctions—twenty-five grades of coat color, three hundred sixty breeds/types.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War reported that the herds had flourished. Horses were classified and named by coat color—twenty-five color grades and three hundred sixty distinct types.

sentences.zh: 其後莊田日增，草場日削，軍民皆困於孳養。

translations.literal: Afterward estate fields daily increased and pasture lands daily shrank—military and civilians alike were trapped in breeding obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter manorial estates spread while pasture shrank, and soldiers and civilians alike were ground down by breeding duties.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，兵部主事湯冕、太僕卿王霽、給事中韓祐、周旋、御史張淳，皆請清核。

translations.literal: Early Hongzhi: Ministry of War clerk Tang Mian, Imperial Stud Director Wang Ji, supervising secretaries Han You, Zhou Xuan, censor Zhang Chun—all requested clearing audits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi, Tang Mian of the Ministry of War, Wang Ji as director of the Imperial Stud, the supervising secretaries Han You and Zhou Xuan, and Censor Zhang Chun all petitioned for a thorough audit.

sentences.zh: 而旋言：「香河諸縣地佔於勢家，霸州等處俱有仁壽宮皇莊，乞罷之，以益牧地。」

translations.literal: Zhou Xuan said: "Land in Xianghe and other counties is occupied by powerful families; Bazhou and other places all have Ren Shou Palace imperial estates—request abolishing them to enlarge pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan added: "Land in Xianghe and neighboring counties has been seized by powerful families, and Bazhou and other districts hold imperial estates of the Renshou Palace. Abolish them and restore the pasture.

sentences.zh: 雖允行，而佔佃已久，卒不能清。

translations.literal: Though approved for execution, occupation and tenancy were long established—in the end could not be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal, but the land had been occupied and leased for too long—it could not be recovered in the end.

sentences.zh: 南京諸衛牧場亦久廢，兵部尚書張鎣請復之。

translations.literal: Nanjing various guards' pastures also long abandoned—Minister of War Zhang Jin requested restoring them.
translations.idiomatic: The pasture lands of the Nanjing guards had also long lain fallow. Minister of War Zhang Jin asked that they be restored.

sentences.zh: 御史胡海言恐遺地利，遂止。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Hai said this would forfeit strategic advantage—so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Hai warned that this would waste strategic ground, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 京師團營官馬萬匹，與旗手等衛上直官馬，皆分置草場。

translations.literal: Capital Garrison Corps official horses ten thousand, together with palace-duty official horses of the Qishou and other guards—all separately placed on pastures.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Garrison Corps kept ten thousand official horses, and the Qishou Guard and other palace-duty units kept their own mounts—all assigned to separate pastures.

sentences.zh: 歲春末，馬非聽用者，坐營官領下場放牧，草豆住支，秋末回。

translations.literal: Each year at late spring, horses not on active duty—the camp officers led them down to pasture; fodder rations suspended; returned at late autumn.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of each spring, horses not on active duty were led to pasture by their camp officers; fodder rations were suspended until they returned in late autumn.

sentences.zh: 給事御史閱視馬斃軍逃者以聞。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors inspected; horses that died and soldiers who fled were reported.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors inspected the herds and reported any dead horses or deserters.

sentences.zh: 後上直馬不出牧，而騎操馬仍歲出如例。

translations.literal: Later palace-duty horses no longer went out to pasture, but cavalry drill horses still went out yearly as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later the palace-duty horses ceased going out to graze, but cavalry drill horses still followed the old seasonal routine.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，武定侯郭勳以邊警為辭，奏免之，徵各場租以充公費，餘貯太僕買馬。

translations.literal: Jiajing 6: Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun, citing frontier alarms, memorialized to exempt them; collected rent from each pasture for public expenses; remainder stored at Imperial Stud to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6 the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, citing frontier alarms, secured an exemption from pasturing; pasture rents were collected for official expenses, with the surplus stored at the Imperial Stud to buy horses.

sentences.zh: 於是營馬專仰秣司農，歲費至十八萬，戶部為詘，而草場益廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon garrison horses relied wholly on the Minister of Revenue's fodder—yearly costs reached one hundred eighty thousand; the Ministry of Revenue was overburdened—and pastures were further abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison horses then depended entirely on the Ministry of Revenue for fodder, at a cost of 180,000 taels a year. The ministry buckled under the strain, and the pastures fell further into disuse.

sentences.zh: 議者爭以租佃取贏，侵淫至神宗時，弊壞極矣。

translations.literal: Advocates competed to profit from rent and tenancy; encroachment continued until Shenzong's reign when corruption reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Officials competed to lease pasture for profit. The encroachment spread until, by Shenzong's reign, the system was ruined beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 茶馬司，洪武中，立於川、陝，聽西番納馬易茶，賜金牌信符，以防詐偽。

translations.literal: Tea-Horse Office: in Hongwu established in Sichuan and Shaanxi; permitted western tribes to offer horses for tea; granted gold plaques and tally tokens to guard against fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The Tea-Horse Office was founded under Hongwu in Sichuan and Shaanxi, allowing western tribes to trade horses for tea. Gold plaques and tally tokens were issued to prevent fraud.

sentences.zh: 每三歲，遣廷臣召諸番合符交易，上馬茶百二十斤，中馬七十斤，下馬五十斤。

translations.literal: Every three years court ministers were dispatched to summon the tribes for tally-matched exchange—upper horse one hundred twenty jin of tea, middle seventy jin, lower fifty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years court envoys summoned the tribes to exchange horses under the tally system: one hundred twenty jin of tea for an upper-grade horse, seventy for a middle-grade horse, fifty for a lower-grade horse.

sentences.zh: 以私茶出者罪死，雖勳戚無貸。

translations.literal: Those who shipped private tea were punishable by death—no exemption even for meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling private tea was a capital crime—no mercy even for the emperor's kin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 末年，易馬至萬三千五百餘匹。

translations.literal: In his later years, horses exchanged reached thirteen thousand five hundred-odd.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the exchange reached more than 13,500 horses.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，禁稍弛，易馬少。

translations.literal: In Yongle the prohibition relaxed slightly; fewer horses exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle enforcement slackened, and fewer horses changed hands.

sentences.zh: 乃命嚴邊關茶禁，遣御史巡督。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered strict frontier tea prohibition; dispatched censors to patrol and supervise.
translations.idiomatic: The court then tightened the frontier tea ban and sent censors to patrol and enforce it.

sentences.zh: 正統末，罷金牌，歲遣行人巡察，邊氓冒禁私販者多。

translations.literal: Late Zhengtong: gold plaques abolished; yearly dispatched envoys to inspect; many frontier commoners violated prohibition and smuggled privately.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhengtong the gold plaques were abolished. Envoys were sent yearly to inspect the trade, but many frontier people defied the ban and smuggled tea on their own.

sentences.zh: 成化間，定差御史一員，領敕專理。

translations.literal: Chenghua: fixed one censor assignment with imperial command to administer exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua one censor was permanently assigned, bearing an imperial mandate to manage the trade exclusively.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，大學士李東陽言：「金牌制廢，私茶盛，有司又屢以敝茶紿番族，番人抱憾，往往以羸馬應。

translations.literal: Hongzhi: Grand Secretary Li Dongyang said: "Gold-plaque system abolished, private tea flourishes; officials repeatedly palmed off worn tea on tribal peoples; tribes nursed resentment and often answered with emaciated horses.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi Grand Secretary Li Dongyang said: "With the gold-plaque system gone, private tea has flourished. Local officials repeatedly pass off spoiled tea on the tribes, who answer in kind with scrawny, worthless horses.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴敕陝西官司揭榜招諭，復金牌之制，嚴收良茶，頗增馬直，則得馬必蕃。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to sternly order Shaanxi officials to post notices and summon compliance, restore the gold-plaque system, strictly collect good tea, and substantially raise horse prices—then horses obtained will surely multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Issue strict orders to Shaanxi officials to post notices and summon the tribes back to the old rules, restore the gold-plaque system, collect only good tea, and raise horse prices generously—then the herds will grow again.

sentences.zh: 及楊一清督理苑馬，遂命並理鹽、茶。

translations.literal: When Yang Yiqing supervised pasture horses, he was ordered to administer salt and tea as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yiqing was put in charge of pasture horses, he was also ordered to oversee salt and tea.

sentences.zh: 一清申舊制，禁私販，種官茶。

translations.literal: Yiqing invoked the old system: forbade private trade and cultivated official tea.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing restored the old regulations: private trade was banned, and official tea plantations were revived.

sentences.zh: 四年間易馬九千餘匹，而茶尚積四十餘萬斤。

translations.literal: In four years they exchanged more than nine thousand horses, while tea still accumulated more than four hundred thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: In four years they traded for more than nine thousand horses, yet more than four hundred thousand jin of tea still sat in store.

sentences.zh: 靈州鹽池增課五萬九千，貯慶陽、固原庫，以買馬給邊。

translations.literal: Lingzhou salt ponds had supplementary levy of fifty-nine thousand, stored in Qingyang and Guyuan treasuries, to buy horses for the border.
translations.idiomatic: An added levy of fifty-nine thousand on the Lingzhou salt pans was banked in the Qingyang and Guyuan treasuries to purchase horses for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又懼後無專官，制終廢也，於正德初，請令巡茶御史兼理馬政，行太僕、苑馬寺官聽其提調，報可。

translations.literal: Fearing that afterward there would be no dedicated officer and the system would in the end be abandoned, at the beginning of Zhengde he requested that the touring tea censor also manage horse policy, with Court of the Imperial Stud and Pasturage Court officials to follow his direction; approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that without a dedicated officer the system would lapse, he asked at the start of Zhengde that the touring tea censor also oversee horse policy, with Imperial Stud and Pasturage Court officers under his direction; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 御史翟唐歲收茶七十八萬餘斤，易馬九千有奇。

translations.literal: Censor Zhai Tang yearly collected more than seven hundred eighty thousand jin of tea and exchanged for more than nine thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhai Tang collected more than seven hundred eighty thousand jin of tea in a year and traded for more than nine thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 後法復弛。

translations.literal: Afterward the law again grew lax.
translations.idiomatic: Later the regulations lapsed once more.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，戶部請揭榜禁私茶，凡引俱南戶部印發，府州縣不得擅印。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, the Ministry of Revenue requested posting proclamations forbidding private tea; all permits were to be issued with the seal of the southern Ministry of Revenue, and prefectures, departments, and counties might not issue them on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing the Ministry of Revenue asked that proclamations forbid private tea trade; all transport permits were to be issued only by the Nanjing ministry, and local governments might not stamp their own.

sentences.zh: 三十年，詔給番族勘合，然初制訖不能復矣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, an edict granted tally-slips to tribal peoples, yet the original system could not in the end be restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year an edict issued tally-slips to frontier tribes, but the original system could never be fully restored.

sentences.zh: 馬市者，始永樂間。

translations.literal: Horse markets began in the Yongle period.
translations.idiomatic: Horse markets date from the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 遼東設市三，二在開原，一在廣寧，各去城四十里。

translations.literal: Liaodong established three markets—two at Kaiyuan and one at Guangning, each forty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong set up three markets—two at Kaiyuan and one at Guangning—each forty li from its garrison town.

sentences.zh: 成化中，巡撫陳鉞復奏行之。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, Grand Coordinator Chen Yue again memorialized to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua, Grand Coordinator Chen Yue memorialized to revive the practice.

sentences.zh: 後至萬曆初不廢。

translations.literal: Afterward, down to the beginning of Wanli, it was not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: It remained in use down to the opening of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，開馬市於大同，陝邊宣鎮相繼行。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, horse markets were opened at Datong; on the Shaanxi frontier Xuanfu and other garrisons followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing, horse markets opened at Datong, and the Xuan and other Shaanxi frontier commands soon followed.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，俺答上表稱貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing, Altan submitted a memorial offering tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing, Altan submitted a memorial professing tributary status.

sentences.zh: 總督王崇古市馬七千餘匹，為價九萬六千有奇。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Chonggu traded for more than seven thousand horses, at a price of more than ninety-six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Chonggu purchased more than seven thousand horses for a price of more than ninety-six thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 其價，遼東以米布絹，宣、大、山西以銀。

translations.literal: The price: in Liaodong, rice, cloth, and silk; in Xuan, Datong, and Shanxi, silver.
translations.idiomatic: Payment in Liaodong was in grain, cloth, and silk; in Xuan, Datong, and Shanxi, in silver.

sentences.zh: 市易外有貢馬者，以鈔幣加賜之。

translations.literal: Apart from market exchange, those presenting tribute horses received additional gifts in paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Horses offered as tribute outside the market received additional rewards in paper currency.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖起江左，所急惟馬，屢遣使市於四方。

translations.literal: At first, when the Taizu rose east of the Yangtze, what he urgently needed was horses alone; he repeatedly sent envoys to purchase them in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor rose in the lower Yangtze, horses were his first need, and he repeatedly sent agents to buy them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 正元壽節，內外籓封將帥皆以馬為幣。

translations.literal: On the Zhengyuan Longevity Festival, enfeoffed princes and generals within and without all took horses as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhengyuan Longevity Festival, imperial kinsmen and commanders inside and outside the capital all presented horses as tribute gifts.

sentences.zh: 外國、土司、番部以時入貢，朝廷每厚加賜予，所以招攜懷柔者備至。

translations.literal: Foreign states, native offices, and tribal departments paid tribute on schedule; the court each time richly added rewards—the means of winning over and soothing were complete in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign states, native chiefs, and frontier tribes sent tribute on schedule, and the court responded with lavish gifts—every device of conciliation was brought to bear.

sentences.zh: 文帝勤遠略，遣使絕域；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was diligent in distant strategy and sent envoys to remote regions;
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzu Emperor, pursuing far-reaching strategy, sent envoys to the ends of the earth;

sentences.zh: 外國來朝者甚眾，然所急者不在馬。

translations.literal: foreign states coming to court were very numerous, yet what was urgently needed was no longer horses.
translations.idiomatic: foreign embassies flocked to court, yet horses were no longer the pressing want.

sentences.zh: 自後狃於承平，駕馭之權失，馬無外增，惟恃孳生歲課。

translations.literal: Afterward, accustomed to long peace, the power to control was lost; horses had no external increase and relied only on yearly breeding levies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, grown complacent in long peace, the court lost its grip on the herds; no fresh stock came from abroad, and it depended only on annual breeding quotas.

sentences.zh: 重以官吏侵漁，牧政荒廢，軍民交困矣。

translations.literal: Compounded by officials' encroachments and exactions, pasture administration fell into ruin, and soldiers and civilians alike were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Official predation piled on top, pasture administration collapsed, and soldiers and civilians alike were ground down.

sentences.zh: 蓋明自宣德以後，祖制漸廢，軍旅特甚，而馬政其一云。

translations.literal: Broadly, from Xuande onward in Ming, ancestral institutions were gradually abandoned; military affairs were especially affected, and horse policy was one instance of this.
translations.idiomatic: In short, from the Xuande reign onward the Ming gradually abandoned ancestral institutions; the military suffered above all, and horse policy was one clear example.
